latest.title: Pemberdayaan UMKM Batik Gama Wening melalui Pengembangan Identitas Merek Berbasis Kearifan Lokal dan Media Pemasaran Digital Berbasis Storytelling
latest.venue: KENDURI Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat
latest.abstract: Batik Gama Wening, a micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) located in Pait Village, Kasembon District, Malang Regency, lacks an adequate brand identity and effective digital marketing management. This community service program aimed to develop a brand identity rooted in local wisdom and enhance the partner's capacity to create storytelling-based digital marketing content to support market expansion. The program involved needs assessment, collaborative brand identity development through a co-creation approach, training in storytelling-based digital marketing content development, outcome-based evaluation, and sustainability enhancement. The program outputs included a logo and corporate color scheme reflecting local characteristics, brand identity applications across supporting media, packaging design, a one-month content calendar, and 12 Instagram content packages. The partner also demonstrated the ability to explain the meaning of the brand identity, plan content themes, develop content using Gemini AI, and prepare materials for publication. Periodic monitoring is necessary to assess the consistency of implementation, the partner's management capacity, and the program's contribution to market expansion and sales transactions.

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: From landlocked to linked: how the China–Europe Railway Express attracts foreign investment
latest.abstract: Purpose International transportation networks are crucial to global capital allocation. This study aims to examine whether and how the China–Europe Railway Express (CR Express) attracts foreign direct investment (FDI) to connected Chinese cities. It identifies the causal effect of railway connectivity on FDI; investigates trade expansion, industrial upgrading and financial development as potential mechanisms; and explores variations across cities with different economic sizes, urban scales and industrial structures. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data for 285 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2003 to 2022, this study treats the staggered launch of the CR Express as a quasi-natural experiment and applies a staggered difference-in-differences model to estimate its effect on inward FDI. Parallel trends test, instrumental-variable tests and other a range of robustness tests assess robustness and endogeneity. Mechanism and heterogeneity analyses examine transmission channels and differences across cities. Findings The research results show that the launching of the CR Express has significantly increased the inflow of FDI to cities along the route. The conclusion is still valid after many robustness tests. Mechanism analysis shows that the CR Express may influence FDI through three potential channels: expanding trade scale, upgrading industrial structure and promoting financial development. Further analysis found that this positive impact is more obvious in economically less-developed cities, service-oriented cities and small- and medium-sized cities. Originality/value This study extends FDI location theory by showing how cross-border railway connectivity can offset inland geographical disadvantages and reshape the spatial distribution of foreign investment. It br

latest.title: An Intelligent Multi-objective Decision Support Model for Sustainable Remanufacturing
latest.venue: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability
latest.abstract: Remanufacturing offers small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) viable pathways towards transitioning to a circular economy; however, intelligent decision-making systems are needed to accelerate its adoption. Balancing the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of sustainability requires the use of analytical tools that can handle multi-dimensional complexity. This study presents a multi-objective optimization model where remanufacturing tasks are allocated to machines in a factory on the basis of minimizing costs, emissions, and noise exposure. Tri-objective optimization has been carried out using the quadrant shrinking method, and Pareto optimal solutions are translated to an implementation framework that can equip SMEs with an intelligent tool for circular economy adoption. In addition to this, we propose an implementation framework for circular economy in manufacturing based on the DMAIC (define, measure, analyze, improve, and control) approach.

latest.title: Customer Retention and Entrenchment Strategies and Competitiveness of Commercial Banks in Nakuru City, Kenya
latest.venue: International Journal of Social Science and Humanities Research (IJSSHR)
latest.abstract: Customer retention and entrenchment strategies are deliberate organizational approaches through which firms sustain long-term customer relationships, reduce switching behaviour and strengthen customer commitment. Commercial banks in Kenya have invested heavily in such strategies, yet intensifying fintech and mobile-money competition, rising customer churn and fluctuating profitability indicate that their contribution to competitiveness remains unclear. The purpose of this study was to examine the effect of customer retention and entrenchment strategies on the competitiveness of commercial banks in Nakuru City, Kenya. Specifically, it assessed the influence of service quality, service personalization, product bundling and digital platforms on competitiveness. The study was anchored on Relationship Marketing Theory, the Resource-Based View, Switching Cost Theory and Customer Lifetime Value Theory. A descriptive correlational research design was adopted. The study targeted 376 managements and customer-facing staff in 62 commercial bank branches in Nakuru City, from which a sample of 111 respondents was drawn using the Nassiuma formula and stratified random sampling. Data were collected through a structured questionnaire, of which 96 were returned (86.5% response rate), and analysed using descriptive statistics and multiple regression. The four strategies jointly explained 62.6% of the variation in competitiveness (R² = 0.626; F = 38.068, p < 0.05). Service quality had the strongest influence (β = 0.460, p < 0.05), followed by digital platforms (β = 0.411, p < 0.05), service personalization (β = 0.277, p < 0.05) and product bundling (β = 0.159, p < 0.05), and all four null hypotheses were rejected. The study concludes that service quality and digital platforms are the princ

latest.title: Prediction markets in the United States: a youth public health perspective
latest.abstract: Prediction markets (PMs) provide the opportunity to trade on the likelihood of an event, such as will Team A beat Team B. PMs are increasingly popular, particularly among young people, because unlike legalized online sports betting, PMs can be accessed in all 50 United States and in some PMs, at age 18. PM's accessibility to young people, gamified features, and strong peer context for transactions contribute to PM popularity among young people, highlighting the urgent need for research on the prevalence of youth PM involvement, youth exposure to PM marketing, and impacts of PM on youth well-being to inform prevention and intervention. This Perspective reviews the distinction between PM and gambling, the appeal of PMs for young people, PM marketing practices that appeal to young people, the developmental context of youth prediction market involvement, and discusses prevention and intervention methods for possible PM-related adverse effects on health among young people.

latest.title: Harnessing multimodal digital markers to advance personalized mental health care: distinguishing trait-like and state-like mechanisms
latest.abstract: Mental health disorders pose a critical global challenge, affecting millions and imposing substantial socio-economic burdens. Traditional one-size-fits-all interventions often fail to capture the complexity of individual mental health trajectories, highlighting the urgent need for more personalized approaches. Digital phenotyping, which leverages multimodal data from smartphones and other sensors, offers a promising avenue for advancing mental health care. However, existing research largely relies on single-modality approaches or “black-box” machine learning (ML) models, limiting both interpretability and clinical applicability. This paper proposes a conceptual framework for integrating multimodal digital markers–including text, acoustic signals, facial expressions, physiological data, and behavioral patterns–with the aim of refining mental health assessment and intervention. A key innovation of this framework is distinguishing between trait-like markers (relatively stable, individual-specific characteristics) and state-like markers (within-individual changes over time). This distinction is crucial for understanding psychopathology and therapeutic change yet remains largely unexamined in existing research. By synthesizing findings across affective, cognitive, and behavioral domains, we demonstrate how automated markers can potentially offer novel insights into mental health mechanisms. The framework implementation flow is illustrated by a clinical demonstration using information from a psychotherapy treatment of an individual diagnosed with depression. Focusing on markers such as vocal tone, facial expressivity, or linguistic features, the trait-like components predict treatment prognosis and state-like components track real-time therapeutic progress. This approach prov

latest.title: Sustainability-Driven Luxury Hotel Choice: The Role of Eco-Consciousness, Sustainable Values, and Fintech Adoption among Young Travellers in Sri Lanka
latest.abstract: This study explores how young travellers understand and interpret sustainability when selecting luxury hotels in Sri Lanka. Specifically, it investigates the meanings and experiences associated with eco-consciousness, perceptions toward eco-sustainability, and eco-sustainable values, while also examining how sustainability initiatives implemented by luxury hotels and fintech-enabled services are perceived within the hotel selection process. By addressing a gap in understanding the lived experiences and perspectives of young travellers, the study contributes to emerging discussions on sustainability-oriented luxury consumption within an emerging tourism destination. Guided by an interpretivist research philosophy and an inductive qualitative approach, the study collected primary data through semi-structured interviews with purposively selected young travellers and luxury hotel managers in Sri Lanka. The research was informed by the Theory of Reasoned Action as a sensitizing theoretical framework. Data were analysed using thematic analysis to identify recurring patterns, perceptions, and meanings associated with sustainable luxury hotel selection. The findings reveal that sustainability is increasingly viewed by young travelers as an integral component of luxury hospitality rather than an optional attribute. Participants associated eco-sustainable practices with authenticity, ethical responsibility, and enhanced travel experiences. Visible sustainability initiatives, environmental transparency, and community-oriented practices emerged as important considerations in hotel evaluations. Fintech-enabled services were perceived as facilitating sustainable travel experiences by improving convenience, transparency, and engagement with sustainability-related initiatives. However,

latest.title: The double-edged sword of virtual influencer anthropomorphism: a paradoxical framework of social presence and identity threat
latest.venue: Journal of Humanities and Applied Social Sciences
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates how the perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers shape consumers’ attitude toward virtual influencers through the competing psychological pathways of social presence and identity threat. Design/methodology/approach Through a cross-sectional survey, a sample of 448 Instagram users in Egypt was collected and analyzed using CB-SEM through AMOS v.23. Findings Both perceived physical and psychological anthropomorphism of virtual influencers have a positive influence on both social presence and identity threat. Importantly, both social presence and identity threat concurrently mediate the relationships between both dimensions of anthropomorphism and attitudes toward virtual influencers. Therefore, both dimensions of anthropomorphism influence consumers’ attitudes toward virtual influencers through the positive mediating role of social presence and the negative mediating role of identity threat. Research limitations/implications The study expands anthropomorphism research to the virtual influencer context by showing that anthropomorphism is not unequivocally superior. Therefore, grounding in social presence and social identity theory, we suggest that anthropomorphism is a double-edged sword in shaping attitudes toward virtual influencers. Practical implications Both designers and marketers employing virtual influencers should consider the multi-dimensionality anthropomorphism. Moreover, they should aim to maximize social presence while reducing identity threat when utilizing virtual influencers. Originality/value This study conceptualizes anthropomorphism as a multifaceted construct composed of physical and psychological dimensions and it can work through two opposing positive and negative pathways.

latest.title: Do Investors Sanction Greenwashing? Selective Market Discipline in Fintech Firms
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT We investigate whether stock market investors detect and penalise greenwashing. We draw on media reports of environmental, social and governance incidents at 321 US‐listed fintech firms between 2007 and 2025, within which greenwashing is identified, following RepRisk, as misleading communication about environmental practice. Investors impose no measurable price penalty when firms are publicly implicated in greenwashing, and the sample is large enough to have detected a penalty of the size observed for other conduct. Misleading communication that does not concern the environment is penalised, where cumulative abnormal returns are between 0.4% and 0.6% lower over the 2 weeks following the report, falling further to 0.8% over the 4 weeks before and after, whereas physical environmental damage draws no adverse reaction. The market therefore prices dishonesty, but the sanction depends on the domain of the false claim, and environmental claims by fintech firms fall outside it. Consistent with stakeholder theory, the results suggest that market‐based discipline exists but is selective, so that the truthfulness of environmental claims cannot be presumed to be enforced by investors where regulatory oversight is absent.

latest.title: Evaluating human-like chatbot interaction in customer service: integrating anthropomorphism and conversational capability
latest.abstract: The development of artificial intelligence (AI)-based technology has driven the development of rule-based chatbots into AI-based chatbots. This development is used by various companies to use AI chatbots as the frontline of customer service. Meeting user expectations for AI chatbots requires an evaluation model to measure chatbot quality. Based on the literature, chatbot evaluation models still focus solely on technical quality, even as AI chatbots are evolving towards human-like services. This research will explore the integration of the technical dimensions of information system success with a new dimension, namely Human-Like Chatbot Interaction (HLCI) as a higher-order construct of anthropomorphism and conversational capability. This quantitative study uses an explanatory research approach. Data were collected through a cross-sectional survey of users of the Veronika chatbot, owned by Telkomsel, an Indonesian telecommunications company. A total of 213 respondents had data ready for analysis using the Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) method in SmartPLS 4, namely the measurement model and structural model tests. The analysis results show that service quality is not significantly related to user satisfaction but has a direct effect on trust. Meanwhile, information quality, system quality, and human-like chatbot interaction are positively related to trust and user satisfaction. Trust and user satisfaction are positively related to intention to continue using. The results of this study can contribute both theoretically and practically to modern AI chatbot quality evaluation models.

latest.title: A transformer-based explainable machine learning framework for heterogeneous ESG risk and return prediction using text intelligence
latest.abstract: Corporate ESG disclosure has shifted toward narrative form, yet vendor ESG ratings that most empirical work depends on show substantial disagreement across providers, and encoders dominant in financial text analysis inherit a 512-token ceiling that discards most of a typical 10-K. HET-ESGFormer combines hierarchical long-document encoding, heterogeneity-aware sparse expert routing conditioned on industry sector and firm size, and a dual-channel explanation layer subject to faithfulness verification. The framework is evaluated on 3,182 U.S.-listed firms over 2015 to 2024 using 10-K filings, sustainability reports, earnings call transcripts, and ESG-tagged news. Against nine baselines spanning econometric, dictionary-based, contextual encoder, sparse-attention, and time-series approaches, HET-ESGFormer reduces return RMSE from 0.0417 to 0.0389 and QLIKE from 0.148 to 0.128, with Diebold-Mariano tests rejecting equal predictive accuracy against every baseline after correction for multiple comparisons. The text channel's marginal contribution to downside risk prediction is materially larger than its contribution to return prediction, widening at longer forecast horizons, indicating that ESG narratives carry more information about risk than about expected return. Ablations reveal a decoupling between predictive skill and explanation faithfulness: removing the consistency regularizer barely affects accuracy but sharply degrades explanation quality. The dual-channel explanation improves ERASER comprehensiveness by 50% over SHAP applied to XGBoost, and human raters significantly prefer the framework's rationales over SHAP-based rationales on trustworthiness. latest.title: L'identité numérique au service de la personnalisation de l'expérience client : un levier de compétitivité pour les entreprises
latest.abstract: Résumé À l’ère du digital, l’identité des consommateurs se construit à travers les données qu’ils génèrent en ligne : profils, historiques d’achats, interactions et comportements numériques. Ces informations constituent une ressource stratégique pour les entreprises, qui les exploitent grâce au Big Data, à l’intelligence artificielle et aux outils CRM afin de proposer des expériences personnalisées. La personnalisation des offres, de la communication et des parcours clients renforce la satisfaction, la fidélisation et la proximité avec la marque. Elle devient ainsi un véritable levier de compétitivité, permettant aux entreprises de se différencier, d’améliorer leur performance marketing et d’optimiser leur productivité. Toutefois, cette dynamique soulève des défis liés à la vie privée, à la confiance numérique et à la régulation des données. Cet article s’attache à comprendre comment l’identité numérique des consommateurs, constituée par l’ensemble des données qu’ils laissent en ligne, peut être utilisée par les entreprises pour concevoir des expériences personnalisées. Il met en évidence les mécanismes par lesquels ces données favorisent l’adaptation des offres, la fidélisation des clients et l’optimisation des stratégies marketing. Il interroge également les retombées de cette personnalisation sur la compétitivité des entreprises, en soulignant à la fois les opportunités d’innovation et les défis liés à la confiance, à la régulation et à l’éthique à l’ère du digital.Mots clés : Identité numérique, Expérience personnalisée, Données clients, Compétitivité des entreprises. Abstract In the digital age, consumer identity is built through the data they generate online: profiles, purchase histories, interactions, and digital behaviors. This information is a strategic resourc

latest.title: The Interplay of Green Intellectual Capital, Artificial Intelligence, Frugal Innovation, and Triple Bottom Line Performance
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The study analyzes the critical role of green intellectual capital (GIC) in enhancing SMEs' economic, social, and environmental performance, with frugal innovation (FI) mediating these relationships. The study also investigates the moderating effect of artificial intelligence (AI) adoption on the relationship between GIC and FI. The hypotheses were tested using PLS‐SEM. Data were collected from 318 manufacturing SMEs operating in three Pakistani cities. Our findings indicate that GIC significantly influences firms' economic, social, and environmental performance in an emerging economy and that FI mediates these relationships. Furthermore, AI adoption strengthens the relationship between GIC and FI. To our knowledge, no previous study has systematically examined GIC, FI, and AI adoption alongside economic, social, and environmental performance, particularly in the context of manufacturing SMEs in an emerging Asian economy. First, this study examines the mediating role of FI in the relationship between GIC and triple bottom line (TBL) performance. Second, it analyzes the moderating role of AI adoption in the relationship between GIC and FI, highlighting the role of technology adoption in strengthening this relationship. Finally, it extends the resource‐based view (RBV) to a technological context by examining how GIC, FI, and AI adoption affect TBL performance.

latest.title: Governance of Hybrid Fintech Ecosystem: An Examination Using the Generativity‐Control Paradigm
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT Digital platforms are increasingly leveraged to address social challenges in the financial sector. However, the fintech sector, particularly in developing economies, is inherently hybrid, creating distinct governance challenges. This study examined the applicability of generativity‐control governance literature to managing dual motives, a federated structure, and a trust‐based value orientation in hybrid fintech ecosystems. Drawing on the digital platform ecosystem governance literature as the theoretical foundation and the concept of holons from information ecology theory as the analytical lens, the study analysed interview data from 41 respondents representing the regulator, ecosystem orchestrator, fintech startups, financial institutions, incubators, and media in the Indian fintech ecosystem. It employed deductive reflexive thematic analysis to analyse the interview data and used secondary data to corroborate the findings. Accordingly, this study conceptualised complementors as holons exhibiting part‐whole behaviour, offering a novel theoretical explanation of how they maintain the generativity‐control balance and address governance challenges to achieve both economic and social outcomes simultaneously in hybrid fintech ecosystems. It also identified and defined three complementary governance mechanisms (demarcation, regulation, and legitimization) that address governance challenges associated with the ecosystem's motives, structure, and value orientation, respectively. Ultimately, the findings extend the information systems governance literature and contribute to the fintech literature by explaining how complementors' collaborative participation, their use of digital public infrastructure, and the provision of regulatory sandboxes within the Indian fintech

latest.title: Seeking Light Within the Shadows: Lessons for Deriving Value from Shadow IT & Shadow AI
latest.venue: Journal of Applied Business and Economics
latest.abstract: Rapid digital innovation often places central information technology organizations (ITOs) at a bottleneck, incentivizing business units to independently deploy 'Shadow IT' solutions to maintain competitive agility. Utilizing systems thinking, this study conceptualizes the tension between decentralized agility and centralized control through the dual feedback loops of user-driven reinforcing motivations and institutional balancing motivations. Methodologically, we employ an exploratory, qualitative multi-site case study of a prominent Research and Development Laboratory, analyzing semi-structured interviews with front-line staff, scientists, business leaders, and the CIO alongside internal organizational artifacts. The thematic analysis reveals five distinct reinforcing motivations that drive end users toward shadow IT—such as perceived task-technology misfit, an autonomous innovation culture, and IT self-sufficiency—and three balancing motivations that guide the ITO to intervene, including cybersecurity mandates and resource optimization. Finally, we outline critical implications for IT leadership to cultivate business-driven IT through persistent dialogue and tiered-trust models, and we explore how the emergent rise of non-deterministic 'Shadow AI' further supercharges these behavioral dynamics.

latest.title: Can agricultural green development policies improve the carbon performance of enterprises? Empirical evidence from listed agricultural enterprises in China
latest.abstract: Introduction Carbon management in agricultural enterprises is deeply embedded in the agricultural industrial ecosystem. The policy of green development in agriculture provides a key path to solve the predicament of carbon reduction in agriculture. Methods This paper, based on the microdata of 245 listed agricultural enterprises in China from 2011 to 2024, uses a dual machine learning model to investigate the impact of agricultural green development policies on the carbon performance (CP) of agricultural enterprises and its mechanism of action. Results The research findings are as follows: First, the green development policy for agriculture has significantly enhanced the CP of agricultural enterprises. Second, mechanism tests have shown that promoting green technological innovation, alleviating financing constraints, and increasing external media attention are the three core paths for agricultural green development policies to enhance the CP of agricultural enterprises. Thirdly, heterogeneity analysis indicates that this policy has a more significant effect on enhancing CP for agricultural enterprises located in the second batch of pilot zones, regions with strong environmental regulations, and those with lower digitalization levels. Fourth, an expansive analysis reveals that there is a significant synergy between the agricultural green development policy and the green finance reform and innovation pilot zone policy in enhancing the CP of agricultural enterprises, and the implementation effect of the compound policy is superior to that of a single policy. Discussion This article expands the research on the environmental effects of agricultural green development policies from the perspective of micro enterprises, providing empirical evidence and policy inspirations for op

latest.title: The Effects of Digital Entrepreneurship, Digital Literacy, and Digital Platforms on Gen Z Purchase Decisions
latest.abstract: The rapid advancement of artificial intelligence (AI) and digital technologies has fundamentally transformed the competitive landscape of micro, small, and medium-sized enterprises (MSMEs). To remain competitive, MSMEs are increasingly required to strengthen their digital entrepreneurial capabilities, improve consumers' digital literacy, and optimize the use of digital platforms. This study examines the effects of digital entrepreneurship, digital literacy, and digital platforms on Generation Z purchase decisions as a strategy for strengthening MSME competitiveness in the era of artificial intelligence. The study employed a quantitative approach involving 175 Generation Z consumers of a local culinary MSME in Bogor, Indonesia. Data were collected through questionnaires and analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with SmartPLS 4. The findings demonstrate that digital entrepreneurship has a positive and significant effect on purchase decisions (β = 0.336, t = 4.040, p < 0.001). Digital literacy also positively and significantly influences purchase decisions (β = 0.205, t = 2.009, p = 0.045), while digital platforms show a positive and significant effect (β = 0.296, t = 3.180, p = 0.001). The model explains 55.8% of the variance in Generation Z purchase decisions. These findings highlight the importance of integrating entrepreneurial digital capabilities, consumer digital literacy, and effective digital platform utilization to enhance MSME competitiveness. In the era of artificial intelligence, these capabilities provide an important foundation for MSMEs to improve market engagement, strengthen consumer decision-making, and sustain their competitiveness in an increasingly technology-driven business environment.

latest.title: Satisfaction, Continuance and Loyalty in Food Delivery Apps: A Bibliometric Analysis of Research, 2016-2026
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Management
latest.abstract: Research on why consumers stay satisfied with, continue using and remain loyal to food delivery apps (FDAs) has grown rapidly, but existing bibliometric reviews rely on single subscription databases and do not publish the search, screening or cleaning steps needed to check them. This study maps that research stream with a fully reproducible protocol. A documented query run in OpenAlex on 14 October 2026 returned 539 records; after logged screening, 420 English-language journal articles published between 2016 and 2026 were analysed. Performance analysis compared full and fractional counting and age-normalised citations. Science mapping combined co-citation analysis with concept co-occurrence analysis based on a published 29-concept thesaurus, Louvain clustering with stability checks and a robustness test on core journals. Output grew by about 40% a year between 2019 and 2025 and has levelled off since 2024. It is concentrated in Indonesia, Malaysia and India, while influence is concentrated in a few early studies. The intellectual base forms one cohesive network rather than distinct schools. At the default resolution, three stable conceptual clusters emerge: service performance and experience, technology acceptance in the COVID-19 period, and relational outcomes; finer resolutions separate an emerging experience-oriented theme. Since the pandemic, attention has shifted from COVID-19 framing towards trust, loyalty, customer experience and delivery performance. Few studies name a theory or use non-survey methods. The findings describe research attention, not causal drivers; practical implications are therefore framed as testable hypotheses for different operating scenarios.

latest.title: Analysis of Religion and Consumption Research
latest.venue: International Journal of Business and Management
latest.abstract: The aim of this study is to identify the general trends of the existing literature on international studies on religion and consumption and to explore the conceptual, intellectual and social structure of the field. For this purpose, 1794 publications searched in the Web of Science database were analysed by bibliometric analysis method. The analysis of the data was carried out with R programming language. Performance analysis and science mapping techniques were applied to analyse the data. According to the findings of the study, the author with the most publications is ‘E.A. Minton’ while ‘O. Sandıkcı’ was the author with the most citations. The journals that publish the most study is ‘Journal of Islamic Marketing’, and the country that produces the most works is ‘USA’. The most cited study is by Muniz and Schau (2005). The most frequently repeated words in the studies were ‘religion’, ‘religiosity’, ‘consumption’, ‘Islam’, ‘consumer behaviour’ and ‘spirituality’. Analysis of keyword co-occurrence network, document and author co-citation network, and author and country collaboration network revealed various clusters. This study presents the general academic structure of the field of religion and consumption and provides a holistic perspective on the field.

latest.title: The Artificial Intelligence and Social Media Marketing Performance: Evidence on Personalization and Predictive Analytics from Pakistan’s Consumer Products Industry
latest.abstract: This study examines how artificial intelligence (AI) affects social media marketing in Pakistan’s consumer products industry, focusing on both its opportunities and its challenges. It uses a mixed-method design that combines 20 in-depth interviews with a structured questionnaire completed by 150 marketing professionals in firms that use AI. Multiple regression analyses show that AI-enabled personalized content and predictive analytics are significant positive predictors of ROI, customer engagement, and conversion rates, and together explain 43% to 50% of the variance in these outcomes. Personalized content is most strongly associated with ROI, while predictive analytics is most strongly associated with conversion rates. The interviews point to three main opportunities: enhanced personalization, greater efficiency and cost savings, and better data-driven decisions. They also point to three main challenges: high implementation costs, data privacy and security concerns, and a shortage of AI skills. The findings highlight the importance of strong data protection, transparency, and staff training for maintaining consumer trust and complying with regulations. The study offers practical recommendations for using AI responsibly in social media marketing. Because the data are cross-sectional, self-reported, and drawn from one industry in one country, the results show associations rather than cause and effect.

latest.title: AI-powered capabilities are associated with green new product development through exploratory and exploitative pathways
latest.abstract: Abstract Purpose – This study aims to investigate the mechanisms through which AI‑powered capabilities influence green NPD in manufacturing firms. Specifically, it examines the dual mediating roles of green exploratory and green exploitative, and tests whether the mediating effect of exploration is stronger than that of exploitation in the AI‑green NPD link. Design/methodology/approach – Drawing on dynamic capabilities theory, this study develops a dual mediation framework distinguishing green exploratory (sensing‑driven opportunity identification) from green exploitative (seizing/transforming‑driven process refinement). Hypotheses are tested using survey data from 333 Chinese manufacturing firms across five high‑priority sectors. Hierarchical regression and bootstrapped mediation analysis (PROCESS Model 4; 5,000 resamples) are employed. Findings – The results show that both green exploratory and green exploitative significantly mediate the positive relationship between AI‑powered capabilities and green NPD. Critically, the indirect effect via green exploratory is significantly stronger than that via green exploitative, supporting asymmetric mediation. The full model explains 54% of the variance in green NPD. Originality/value – This study makes three key contributions. First, it unpacks the mediation black box between AI and green NPD by specifying two distinct process architectures. Second, it challenges the “balance assumption” of ambidexterity theory by demonstrating the primacy of exploratory mediation in AI‑enabled green innovation contexts, thereby extending dynamic capabilities theory. Third, it provides a rigorous methodological template for testing dual and asymmetric mediation, offering actionable guidance for managers, AI vendors, and policymakers.

latest.title: Too little, too much, or just right? How AI recommendation information volume shapes trust and consumer behavior
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) shopping assistants explain why a product is selected, yet the appropriate defaults remain unclear. We define recommendation information volume as the amount of nonredundant, product-relevant information and compare five ordered explanation packages. Study 1 identifies an inverted-U response in a randomized Chinese mobile-retail experiment. Study S1 compares identical messages attributed to an AI assistant or a human salesperson, with separate source-neutral measurement validation. Study 2 reports conditional positive indirect associations through perceived usefulness, trust in AI, and decision comfort, and conditional negative indirect associations through information overload and algorithmic over-justification. Same-session estimates do not establish causal mediation. Its product-version comparison combines complexity, functionality, and safety considerations. Study 3 provides behavioral evidence across 51,248 recommendation impressions and service outcomes for 5000 distinct users. Moderate packages perform best within the tested sets. Bounded information processing explains the benefit–burden trade-off; persuasion knowledge suggests that disproportionate justification depends on expectations of selective versus comprehensive advice, across AI and human sources. Because amount, diagnostic priority, and content composition vary jointly, the experiments identify assigned-package effects, not pure quantity effects. The findings support category-specific testing of default explanations without establishing an exclusively algorithmic mechanism.

latest.title: Creating satisfaction and loyalty among tourists: the power of experiential tourism
latest.abstract: Abstract The current research examines whether experiential tourism activities in the tourism industry can influence tourists’ behaviour. Using the stimulus-organism-response framework, the study examines how experience affects travellers’ intentions for satisfaction and loyalty among online travel agents (OTAs). Data were collected from 208 visitors across five travel destinations in India, specifically wildlife sanctuaries and national parks, to examine their lived experiences. The results were analysed using a partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) approach, indicating that experiential tourism indicators have a direct effect on customer engagement. The study suggests that experiential motivation is vital in shaping tourists’ satisfaction and loyalty. The results suggest that tourists are more likely to return to the OTA and recommend it to others if they have positive experiential motivation during their travel encounter. Moreover, the study highlights the importance of co-creation in the tourism industry. In the challenging competitive space, leveraging experiential strategies can help managers gain a competitive advantage. Travel retailers must focus on increasing tourists’ conscious participation and include certain activities that may motivate them and create enthusiasm. This study is one of the few in India to explore the relationship between experiential activities and tourist satisfaction and loyalty among wildlife sanctuaries and national parks travellers.

latest.title: Dynamic Capabilities, Organizational Resilience, Digital Transformation and Organizational Performance of Deposit-Taking Saccos in Nairobi County, Kenya
latest.venue: Journal of Economics Finance and Management Studies
latest.abstract: This study examined the influence of dynamic capabilities on the organizational performance of deposit-taking SACCOs in Nairobi County, Kenya, and tested the mediating role of organizational resilience and the moderating role of digital transformation. Given the importance of SACCOs and the various challenges they face from digital disruption and regulation, this study aims to investigate the impact of dynamic capabilities on the performance of SACCOs in Kenya’s Nairobi County. The survey design was used to collect data directly from the SACCO managers in the study areas. Out of the 240 questionnaires distributed, 210 yielded usable responses for the study, giving the study an 87.50% response rate. The data were collected using five-point Likert scales and analyzed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, hierarchical regression, Hayes PROCESS Models 4 (mediation), 1 (moderation), 14 (moderated mediation), and 59 (second-stage moderated mediation). The findings of the study revealed that dynamic capabilities had a positive and significant effect on organizational performance. Furthermore, dynamic capabilities significantly enhanced the organizational resilience of these SACCOs, and the organizational resilience significantly improved their organizational performance. Additionally, digital transformation significantly predicted their organizational performance. The study also established that organizational resilience partially mediated the relationship between dynamic capabilities and the performance of these SACCOs. The index for moderated mediation was significant, as digital transformation significantly moderated the relationship between dynamic capabilities and the organizational performance of these SACCOs. latest.title: INFLUENCER CREDIBILITY AND TRAVEL DECISION-MAKING AMONG YOUNG GEN Z SOCIAL MEDIA USERS IN PENANG
latest.venue: Quantum Journal of Social Sciences and Humanities
latest.abstract: Social media has become a significant influence on consumer decisions worldwide, including decisions about where and how to travel. Drawing on the source credibility model, this study examined the relationship between three influencer credibility dimensions, attractiveness, trustworthiness and expertise; and travel decision-making among young Generation Z (Gen Z) social media users in Pulau Pinang, Malaysia. A total of 266 respondents aged 18 to 28 were recruited using non-probability purposive sampling, supported by online snowball distribution through university and young-adult networks. Data were collected through a self-administered online questionnaire adapted from established credibility scales and analysed using descriptive statistics, Pearson correlation, and multiple linear regression. All three dimensions correlated positively and significantly with travel decision-making at the bivariate level. In the regression model, the three dimensions jointly explained 54.3 per cent of the variance, F(3, 262) = 103.68, p < .001. Expertise emerged as the strongest predictor (β = .49, p < .001), followed by attractiveness (β = .23, p < .001), while trustworthiness made no significant unique contribution (β = .10, p = .165), a result attributable to its strong correlation with expertise (r = .80). The achieved sample was predominantly female (82.0 percent), aged 18 to 24 (91.7 percent), and not in paid employment (83.8 percent); the findings therefore characterise this specific segment of young, highly engaged Gen Z social media users rather than the Gen Z population of Pulau Pinang as a whole. The study extends understanding of influencer credibility in a Malaysian travel context and indicates that destination marketers targeting young Gen Z audiences should prioritise dem

latest.title: The Impact of Audit on Good Governance in Dimen Shoring Incorporated: Basis for Compliance and Transparency
latest.venue: World Journal of Sustainable Advances in Multidisciplinarity
latest.abstract: This study assessed employee perceptions of the impact of audit practices on good governance in Dimen Shoring Incorporated – Calamba, Laguna Branch. Using a quantitative-descriptive research design, data were collected from 105 employees through a close-ended survey questionnaire and analyzed using weighted means. The findings indicated that employees strongly agreed that internal audit practices (overall weighted mean = 3.68), external audit practices (3.66), compliance audit procedures (3.67), and audit frequency and follow-up implementation (3.69) were effectively practiced and contributed to organizational improvement. Results further showed that good governance was strongly perceived in the workplace, particularly in accountability (3.75), compliance with policies and regulations (3.76), ethical management and resource utilization (3.70), and transparency (3.67). The study concluded that employees perceived auditing as a valuable mechanism that supports governance outcomes through strengthened compliance, accountability, transparency, and ethical management. Recommendations focused on improving communication of audit results, enhancing follow-up visibility, strengthening audit procedure orientation, improving decision-related transparency, and reinforcing ethical culture initiatives.

latest.title: Analyzing Consumer Loyalty to Ultra‐Fast Fashion: An Integrative Analysis Based on the Stimulus‐Organism‐Response Model
latest.abstract: ABSTRACT The ultra‐fast fashion industry generates massive online sales, partly because of its ability to attract the custom of Generation Z (Gen Z). Given that this generational cohort typically has low brand loyalty, this paper examines how the dimensions of the stimulus‐organism‐response (S‐O‐R) model explain Gen Z's loyalty to the ultra‐fast fashion industry. For this purpose, the analysis presented in this paper relies on both a linear and an evolutionary view of the S‐O‐R model. Based on data from 208 questionnaires completed by consumers of ultra‐fast fashion, two analytical phases were conducted: (1) partial least squares structural equation modeling (PLS‐SEM) and (2) qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). The results of the first phase suggest that consumer sustainability consciousness is associated with brand loyalty directly and under mediation, whereas social media peer communication is associated with brand loyalty only under mediation by brand equity. The second phase shows the relevance of brand equity in explaining both high and low brand loyalty. The configurations explaining high brand loyalty or low brand loyalty show that the relationship of each outcome with consumer sustainability consciousness and social media peer communications reflects psychological mechanisms that allow consumers to overcome the cognitive dissonance between their attitudes and behavior.

latest.title: Komunikasi Bisnis Berbasis AI: Analisis Ketegangan antara Efisiensi Teks Generatif dan Degradasi Otentisitas Brand Voice pada UMKM
latest.venue: Equivalent Journal Of Economic Accounting and Management
latest.abstract: Perkembangan AI generatif menawarkan efisiensi produksi konten pemasaran bagi UMKM, namun memunculkan masalah berupa keseragaman linguistik, hilangnya identitas merek, dan berkurangnya kedekatan emosional. Penelitian ini bertujuan menganalisis karakteristik bahasa AI dalam komunikasi pemasaran UMKM, bentuk intervensi manusia melalui pendekatan Human-in-the-Loop (HITL), serta implikasinya terhadap kepercayaan konsumen. Penelitian kualitatif ini menggunakan metode analisis isi terhadap teks pemasaran AI dan draf modifikasi pelaku usaha. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa teks bawaan AI cenderung homogen, klise, dan kurang mencerminkan konteks budaya lokal. Sebaliknya, intervensi manusia melalui penyesuaian gaya bahasa, humor, adaptasi budaya, dan storytelling terbukti efektif memperkuat identitas merek dan kedekatan dengan audiens. Temuan juga mengindikasikan bahwa konsumen semakin mampu mengenali konten generik, sehingga autentisitas menjadi faktor krusial. Disimpulkan bahwa komunikasi bisnis yang efektif di era AI memerlukan kolaborasi yang memadukan efisiensi draf mesin dengan kapasitas empati dan makna dari manusia. Oleh karena itu, pendekatan HITL menjadi strategi esensial bagi UMKM untuk mempertahankan autentisitas dan meningkatkan kepercayaan konsumen.

latest.title: Integrating the Technology Acceptance Model and Hifz al-Mal: Digital Financial Literacy and Digital Payment Adoption in Shaping Financial Behaviour
latest.venue: International Journal of Academic Research in Business and Social Sciences
latest.abstract: The rapid growth of digital financial technologies has reshaped the global payment landscape, contributing to the shift toward a cashless society. While digital payment platform offers greater convenience and efficiency, they can also affect how individuals manage their finances and make spending decisions. This study examines the influence of digital financial literacy and digital payment adoption on responsible financial behaviour by integrating Technology Acceptance Model (TAM) with the Islamic principle of Hifz al-Mal (protection of wealth). Using a quantitative research design, data were collected among 210 university students who actively use digital payment platforms. The study employs Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modelling (PLS-SEM) to examine the proposed research model. The findings reveal that digital payment usage has a positive and significant effect on financial behaviour and digital financial literacy emerged as the strongest predictor. This study contributes theoretically by integrating TAM and Hifz al-Mal into the domain of financial behaviour and highlighting the critical role of digital financial behaviour as both a driver and a protective mechanism against financial risk.

latest.title: The Taxation of Non-Resident Digital Service Providers Without Physical Presence In Tanzania: Jurisdictional and Enforcement Challenges
latest.venue: East African Journal of Law and Ethics
latest.abstract: The study examines the jurisdictional and enforcement challenges associated with taxing non-resident digital service providers without physical presence in Tanzania. The rapid growth of the digital economy has enabled non-resident providers to supply digital services to Tanzanian consumers without establishing conventional physical premises in the country, creating challenges for traditional tax rules based on physical presence. The study adopts doctrinal and non-doctrinal legal research methodologies. The doctrinal approach analyses relevant tax legislation, subsidiary legislation, policy documents, international tax materials and scholarly literature, while the non-doctrinal approach draws on empirical information obtained from selected respondents and interviews with Tanzania Revenue Authority tax officials. The study is guided by the Ability to Pay Theory, Benefit Theory and Neutrality Theory. The findings indicate that jurisdictional challenges include difficulties in establishing a taxable nexus, determining the location of digital transactions and consumers, accessing information held outside Tanzania, and exercising taxing authority over providers operating across borders. The study further finds that enforcement is constrained by difficulties in identifying and monitoring non-resident providers, obtaining reliable transaction information, reliance on voluntary compliance, limitations in monitoring payment systems, technological and data-integration challenges, and difficulties in enforcing tax liabilities against providers located outside Tanzania. The study concludes that although Tanzania has established a legal and administrative framework for taxing non-resident digital service providers, its effectiveness is constrained by practical jurisdictional and enfo

latest.title: A Study on the Research Description Development at Grand View Research
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: Research Description (RD) development requires the conversion of extensive market information into a concise, accurate and client-facing overview. This case study examines the role of secondary market research in RD creation and updating at Grand View Research (GVR), based on the author’s on-the-job training in the Product Development Team. The study follows a descriptive case-study design using internship observations and publicly available secondary information; no primary survey was conducted. During the training, more than 450 RDs were updated, and more than 50 were created from scratch across multiple industry verticals. The observed workflow included assignment understanding, market and report review, information synthesis, RD drafting, self-quality control, mentor review, revision, and progression to editing and publication. A focused case of artificial intelligence (AI) in marketing within the Consumer Goods segment illustrates how global, segment-level and country-level market information can be synthesized while preserving differences in scope. The study finds that RD quality depends on source relevance and authority, consistency of definitions and numbers, selective synthesis, and human quality control. It recommends a standardized RD checklist, a structured knowledge repository and carefully governed AI-assisted checks with human validation.

latest.title: Significance of OTT platforms and challenges faced by the Pakistani film industry
latest.abstract: This paper examines the position of local Over-The-Top (OTT) platforms in Pakistan such as Tamasha, SeePrime, Tapmad, and UrduFlix and the issues they encounter in the changing media environment in Pakistan. These sites have revolutionized the way viewers (especially the younger ones) watch movies and plays by offering them the convenience of on-demand viewing. They have also provided a platform to filmmakers to present a variety of stories and spread Pakistani culture beyond conventional cinemas. Along with these opportunities, the Pakistani OTT platforms have a number of challenges that restrain its growth. They cannot fulfil the demands of the audience because of low budget, censorship, piracy, weak internet connection, and inadequate technology. Most of the viewers want quality productions yet they want them to be free or pirated, which makes the local platforms even weaker in terms of revenue. The research was quantitative in nature, since it entailed survey of OTT users and media professionals in Pakistan. The survey findings indicate that most of the younger audiences are moving towards the digital platforms, which they find convenient and diverse. Nevertheless, the respondents also pointed to the poor quality and affordability of local services in comparison to international ones. The results indicate that Pakistani OTT platforms need to enhance the quality of productions, invest in low-cost subscriptions, and invest in digital infrastructure so that they can survive and succeed. All these can be addressed by local platforms which can aid in revival of the Pakistani film industry and make it relevant in the digital world.

latest.title: Strategic Cooperation Between the State and Business in the Tourism Industry
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to develop directions for improving the organisational and economic mechanisms of public–private partnership in Ukraine’s tourism sector, based on a comparison with international practice and an analysis of regional tourism tax revenues from 2021 to 2024. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study examines public-private partnership mechanisms in tourism infrastructure development and destination management. It combines a narrative review of 32 purposively selected publications (2021–2025) with official statistics for 24 regions of Ukraine; the research instrument was an analytical matrix of five partnership dimensions, and data were analysed using comparative and trend analyses. Research Limitation: The proposed mechanisms, derived from secondary data, have not been empirically validated. Findings: Effective government–business interaction in tourism depends on a clear distribution of responsibilities, the integration of environmental and social criteria into partnership projects, and the institutionalisation of local community participation. These factors strengthen investment effectiveness, improve destination management, and enhance the long-term sustainability of tourism development. Practical Implication: The findings provide guidance for improving tourism policy, designing effective public-private partnership models, and strengthening the governance of tourism destinations. Social Implication: Strengthened cooperation between the public and private sectors contributes to sustainable tourism, greater community engagement, and balanced regional development. Originality/Value: The study proposes an integrated framework for enhancing organisational and economic mechanisms of state–business cooperation by incorporating sustainable development prin

latest.title: Digital Transformation of MSMEs in Southwest Nigeria: The Interactive Effects of Infrastructure, Digital Skills, and Policy Environment on Adoption and Firm Performance
latest.venue: International Journal of Modern Science and Research Technology
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study explored the digital transformation of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) in Southwest Nigeria by investigating the effects of digital infrastructure, digital skills, policy environment, and their interaction on digital adoption and firm performance. The study addressed a gap in the literature by evaluating the possibility of the determinants working independently or in complement to each other in influencing the MSME digital transformation. Methodology: The mixed method research design was used by collecting quantitative data from 240 MSMEs in Lagos, Ogun, Oyo and Ekiti States, while qualitative data was gathered through key informant interviews and focus group discussions. Descriptive statistics, Pearson correlations and Generalized Linear Models (GLM) were used for analyzing quantitative data, and thematic analysis of NVivo software was used for analyzing qualitative data. Findings: The results show that digital infrastructure is the strongest determinant of digital adoption, followed by digital skills and policy environment. The interaction effects of digital infrastructure and digital skills, digital skills and policy environment, and digital infrastructure and policy environment were statistically significant, showing that these factors are complementary and mutually reinforcing. Furthermore, digital adoption, digital infrastructure, digital skills, and policy environment significantly improve MSME performance. These findings suggest that coordinated investments across all three areas yield greater returns than isolated interventions. The study reveals that digital transformation in MSMES in Southwest Nigeria is attributed to the synergistic effect of digital infrastructure, digital capabilities and policy interventions. latest.title: The Legal Framework for Digital Lending by Tier 2 Microfinance Service Providers in Tanzania: Assessing Applicability and Enforcement Challenges
latest.venue: International Journal of Law Management & Humanities
latest.abstract: Digital lending through mobile applications has become a major source of credit for individuals and small traders in Tanzania, but it has been accompanied by high and poorly disclosed costs, the harvesting of borrowers’ telephone data and abusive methods of debt collection. This article examines the legal framework that regulates digital lending by non-deposit-taking (Tier 2) microfinance service providers in Mainland Tanzania and asks whether that framework is applicable to the lenders it is meant to govern and capable of being enforced against them. Using doctrinal legal research supplemented by a limited comparison with Kenya, it analyses the Microfinance Act, the Microfinance (Non-Deposit Taking Microfinance Service Providers) Regulations, 2019, the Bank of Tanzania (Financial Consumer Protection) Regulations, 2019, the Guidelines on Fees and Charges, 2024, the Guidance Note on Digital Lenders, 2024, the Personal Data Protection Act, the Electronic Transactions Act and the National Payment Systems Act, and evaluates them against the public interest theory of regulation, the distinction between entity-based and activity-based regulation, and responsive regulation. The article finds that the rules specific to digital lending are contained in a guidance note rather than in regulations, although the Microfinance Act empowers the Bank of Tanzania to make regulations on digital microfinance business; that the price of credit is controlled by disclosure alone; that the binding rules on personal data and debt collection are general and fragmented, with inconsistent sanctions; and that the conduct rules bind only licensed providers, leaving unlicensed and foreign-hosted lenders largely outside the framework. latest.title: The Use of Artificial Intelligence in the Tourism Business
latest.abstract: Purpose: To examine the use of artificial intelligence in the tourism industry and evaluate its impact on operational efficiency and service quality in the context of smart tourism. Design/Methodology/Approach: The study combines an analysis of 32 tourism enterprises operating in the European market with a survey of 124 consumers conducted in 2024–2025. Artificial intelligence adoption was assessed through the level of operational process automation, and content analysis of enterprise reports and platform analytics was used to measure performance before and after implementation. Research Limitation: The study is limited to European tourism enterprises and a relatively small consumer sample. Future research should include broader geographical coverage and longitudinal analysis. Findings: Artificial intelligence significantly improved operational performance. Average service time decreased from 18.6 to 11.2 minutes, automation increased from 27.4% to 61.8%, and customer interaction intensity rose from 1.8 to 2.6 contacts per user. Consumers reported high satisfaction with service quality and personalisation, although trust in intelligent systems remained moderate, indicating that behavioural barriers still constrain the full benefits of AI adoption. Practical Implication: The findings support the adoption of hybrid service models that combine artificial intelligence with human interaction. Social Implication: Effective AI implementation can improve service accessibility, customer satisfaction, and the sustainable development of smart tourism. Originality/Value: The novelty lies in an integrated model linking the share of AI-automated processes with operational variables (service time, customer contacts) and consumer variables (service quality, personalisation, trust).

latest.title: AI capacities and digital entrepreneurship: The moderating role of Fintech entrepreneurial ecosystems and university infrastructure
latest.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is reshaping digital entrepreneurship by supporting business decision making, digital planning, customer analysis, and process automation. However, the mechanisms through which students’ perceived AI capacities relate to digital entrepreneurial self-efficacy and digital entrepreneurial intention remain insufficiently theorized. Drawing on Social Cognitive Career Theory (SCCT), this study examines whether digital entrepreneurial self-efficacy mediates the association between AI capacities and digital entrepreneurial intention, and whether FinTech entrepreneurial ecosystems and university infrastructure condition these relationships. Based on cross-sectional survey data from 1061 higher education students in Vietnam, the results show that AI capacities are positively associated with digital entrepreneurial self-efficacy, which in turn is positively associated with digital entrepreneurial intention. Crowdfunding is associated with a stronger AI capacities–self-efficacy association, whereas mobile payment shows a negative moderating association and blockchain shows no significant moderation. University entrepreneurial environment and entrepreneurial program learning positively—though modestly—moderate the examined associations. Because the study applies an efficacy-centered, partial specification of SCCT to cross-sectional data, all findings are interpreted as associations rather than causal effects. These findings contribute to technology-enabled entrepreneurship research by linking user-centric AI capacities with financial and institutional boundary conditions in an emerging-market context. hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments.
