latest.title: Defying the odds: the relative age effect's absence among the best teenage football players in the world
latest.venue: Frontiers in Sports and Active Living
latest.abstract: Abstract The relative age effect (RAE) is the advantage of being born earlier than others in the selection period, being more experienced and more developed. It has been suggested that, among the best athletes, the RAE might inverse due to relatively younger players struggling more and thus developing different, more robust, skill sets. Recently, the CIES Football Observatory selected the world’s 200 best teenage football players, using objective measures such as minutes played - weighted by sporting level, transfer value, and an in-game performance index. That sample of players enabled testing whether they are truly different from top performers in youth competitions, and whether the RAE might even inverse at the top level. To that end, in a natural experiment, birth date distributions across quartiles of the 200 CIES’s list players were compared with the corresponding distributions of players participating in the most recent FIFA U-20 World Cups, in Chile in 2025 ( N = 504) and in Argentina in 2023 ( N = 504). The birth date distributions, between the CIES’ 200 and the 2025 FIFA U20WC, significantly differed from each other, χ 2 (3, N = 704) = 34.3336, p < .00001, as did distributions between the CIES’ 200 and players in the 2023 FIFA U20WC, χ 2 (3, N = 704) = 19.3969, p < .0003. The latter two samples were similar. The results indicate that while the RAE is advantageous for those at the highest level of youth football, it has not helped those who have developed into world-class senior players.

latest.title: PENDAMPINGAN TRANSFORMASI DIGITAL MELALUI PENGEMBANGAN DAN IMPLEMENTASI WEBSITE EDOTEL DI SMK NEGERI 2 GORONTALO
latest.abstract: SMK Negeri 2 Gorontalo memiliki edOTEL sebagai unit hotel latih yang berfungsi sebagai sarana pembelajaran praktik bagi siswa Kompetensi Keahlian Perhotelan. Namun, pengelolaan edOTEL masih menghadapi kendala berupa promosi konvensional, pencatatan reservasi kamar secara manual, dan latihan praktik front office berbasis dokumen kertas. Kondisi tersebut menyebabkan proses administrasi kurang efisien dan belum optimal dalam mendukung kesiapan siswa menghadapi sistem perhotelan digital. Kegiatan pengabdian kepada masyarakat ini bertujuan mengembangkan, menyosialisasikan, dan mengimplementasikan website edOTEL yang mengintegrasikan fungsi promosi, manajemen reservasi berbasis web, dan e-learning simulasi praktik front office. Kegiatan dilaksanakan selama Mei–Juli 2026 dengan melibatkan 58 peserta, terdiri atas 8 guru/pengelola dan 50 siswa Kompetensi Keahlian Perhotelan. Metode pelaksanaan menggunakan pendekatan Participatory Action Learning yang dipadukan dengan Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) model Waterfall, meliputi analisis kebutuhan, perancangan, pengembangan dan pengujian, pelatihan, serta evaluasi. Hasil kegiatan menunjukkan bahwa landing page, sistem manajemen reservasi, modul e-learning front office, serta sosialisasi dan distribusi panduan digital mencapai ketercapaian 100%, sedangkan integrasi payment gateway mencapai 60%. Evaluasi terhadap 58 responden menunjukkan tingkat penerimaan dan kelayakan sistem sebesar 87,91% dengan kategori sangat layak. Dengan demikian, website edOTEL mampu meningkatkan efisiensi administrasi dan promosi serta mendukung pembelajaran digital terapan dalam ekosistem Teaching Factory

latest.title: Design and analysis of an intelligent audit risk assessment system based on retrieval-augmented large language model
latest.abstract: Audit risk assessment is increasingly challenged by complex financial environments and the limited ability of traditional data-driven models to capture contextual information. Existing approaches mainly depend on structured financial indicators and often overlook regulatory knowledge and narrative disclosures. This study proposes an intelligent audit risk assessment framework that integrates a retrieval-augmented large language model (RAG-LLM) with a Bayesian–logistic hybrid estimation mechanism. The framework integrates financial, governance, operational, and textual data with audit standards, regulatory cases, and historical accounting irregularities to support context-aware risk evaluation. The proposed system was evaluated using an economically calibrated synthetic dataset consisting of 612 firm-year observations across 14 industries from 2018 to 2024. Results show that the RAG–LLM Bayesian hybrid model achieves an out-of-sample AUC of 0.912, outperforming gradient boosting (0.754), random forest (0.723), and logistic regression (0.694). It also achieves improved calibration performance with a Brier score of 0.088 and a misclassification rate of 6.7%. Further analysis shows that LLM-derived reasoning constructs contribute 48.3% of the total explanatory contribution. The findings demonstrate that retrieval-enhanced reasoning improves prediction accuracy, interpretability, and decision support capability for intelligent auditing systems.

latest.title: Mapping industrial and organizational psychology research and its alignment with the changing world of work: A topic modeling review
latest.abstract: The world of work is changing rapidly due to digitalization, economic shifts and environmental concerns. To examine whether industrial and organizational (I-O) psychology research reflects these changes, we analyzed 10,552 abstracts published in 20 leading journals between 2015 and 2025 using neural topic modeling (BERTopic) and compared them with research from 2005 to 2014. We identified 74 topics, grouped into 16 macro-themes, and measured how closely 24 emerging changes described by the World Economic Forum and recent I-O literature are represented in these topics. The core of the field, including personnel assessment, leadership, careers and job demands, remained stable over two decades, while research on diversity, inclusion and well-being expanded. Research on artificial intelligence grew almost tenfold but focused mainly on its use in human resource management. Changes concerning employees and their well-being were well represented, whereas wider changes in the economy and the labor market, such as the gig economy, reskilling and climate change, remained peripheral. Research on these changes exists but is scattered and often does not form distinct topics. We outline directions for research that addresses the changing world of work more directly.
keywords: artificial intelligence in human resource management

latest.title: The relationship between green human resources management (GHRM) and service quality
latest.venue: Silphium Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: In recent decades, human activities have increasingly negatively impacted the environment, driven by factors such as globalization and intensifying competition. In response, a modern approach to Human Resource Management (HRM), known as Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), has emerged. GHRM aims to integrate eco-friendly practices into organizational operations while maintaining business competitiveness. This study contributes to the existing body of knowledge by exploring the impact of GHRM on service quality within small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Tripoli, Libya. A quantitative research methodology was adopted, with data collected through a survey administered to a randomly selected sample of 100 employees working in various SMEs in Tripoli. Ethical approval was obtained from the relevant Libyan authorities, and the surveys were distributed both electronically and in person, in compliance with institutional permissions. The collected data were analyzed using multiple regression analysis to test the study’s hypotheses. The findings indicate that employees in Libyan SMEs possess a moderate understanding of GHRM practices. Furthermore, the results demonstrate a statistically significant positive relationship between GHRM and service quality. Based on these findings, the study recommends that service-oriented industries prioritize the adoption of GHRM practices to enhance service performance, improve organizational outcomes, and promote environmental sustainability.

latest.title: Sometimes less is more: A real options view on minority acquisitions by family firms
latest.abstract: Acquisitions involve high uncertainty, as firms commit substantial resources long before the performance outcomes of these investments are known. Drawing on real options logic, firms may prefer minority acquisitions over majority acquisitions because minority stakes secure strategic options while reducing exposure to risk. We examine this assumption in the context of family firms, whose desire to preserve socioemotional wealth (SEW), alongside financial returns, leads them to make strategic choices that differ from those of non-family firms. Based on a panel dataset of U.S. S&P 500 firms, we find that, through their prioritization of SEW (e.g., independence, binding social ties, and family identity and reputation), family firms are more likely than non-family firms to undertake minority acquisitions and to make a follow-up acquisition after an initial minority acquisition. Furthermore, family firms’ prioritization of SEW (e.g., emotional attachment and binding social ties) leads to a higher inclination toward industry-related minority acquisitions.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Depression, anxiety, stress, and intolerance of uncertainty during the COVID-19 pandemic by considering the impact of pre-existing mental health issues
latest.abstract: Purpose This research was conducted during the COVID-19 pandemic. This study aims to investigate self-reported mental health issues in a public sample, including depression, anxiety and intolerance of uncertainty about the future. Design/methodology/approach A public sample (N = 313) was obtained through social media, and collected using an online survey. Participants completed a series of demographic questions including disclosure about previous mental health issues, the depression anxiety stress scale (DASS) and the intolerance uncertainty scale (IUS). Findings There was a strong positive relationship between elements of the DASS and IUS. Having previous mental health issues were strongly associated with higher scores across all measures. Originality/value Evidence is provided to support the notion that additional stress, anxiety and fear is experienced by people with pre-existing mental health issues during unprecedented times. This research offers a unique insight into the mental health of the general public during a global pandemic.

latest.title: Challenges Faced by Parents in Raising Children with Special Needs: A Narrative Literature Review
latest.venue: Journal Of Education And Teaching Learning (JETL)
latest.abstract: Parents raising children with special needs face interconnected psychological, physical, social, financial, and service-related challenges. This narrative literature review aimed to synthesize evidence on parental difficulties, influencing factors, coping strategies, and support needs. Fifteen empirical studies published between 2019 and 2026 were selected through eligibility screening and qualitative appraisal. Data were extracted using a structured matrix and analyzed through thematic narrative synthesis. The findings showed that parents commonly experienced emotional distress, fatigue, stigma, social isolation, financial pressure, employment disruption, family strain, and limited access to healthcare, rehabilitation, and inclusive education. The severity of these challenges was shaped by the child’s condition, parental knowledge, coping capacity, family support, socioeconomic status, cultural beliefs, geographical location, and service accessibility. Parents used acceptance, information seeking, spiritual practices, advocacy, structured routines, and social support. The review highlights the need for continuous family-centered services integrating psychological, educational, financial, professional, workplace, and policy support. Ultimately, establishing robust policy frameworks and fostering cross-sectoral collaboration among healthcare providers, educators, and community leaders are essential to mitigate systemic barriers, alleviate caregiver burnout, and promote holistic family resilience. Furthermore, future empirical research must prioritize longitudinal methodologies to evaluate the sustainable real-world efficacy, accessibility, and scalability of culturally tailored intervention programs across diverse socioeconomic landscapes.
keywords: parents of children with special needs

latest.title: Supply chain networks in horticulture: an assessment of farmers' perceptions and market linkages
latest.venue: Modern Supply Chain Research and Applications
latest.abstract: Purpose This study investigates the determinants of horticulture supply chain efficiency (SCE) and the mediating effects of market linkage strength (MLS). Design/methodology/approach The study conceptualises and tests a partial least squares structural equation modelling model based on the resource-based view and relational exchange theory, with the data collected from 500 horticultural farmers from Shimla, Kullu and Kinnaur districts of Himachal Pradesh. Findings The findings show that logistics capability (LC) has the strongest effects on MLS (β = 0.395) and SCE (β = 0.388), followed by information and coordination (IC). Transaction fairness (TF) and digital adoption (DA) significantly strengthen MLS, while MLS positively influences SCE (β = 0.233). MLS provides complementary mediation for LC and IC and indirect-only mediation for TF and DA. Originality/value The study integrates operational capabilities and relational mechanisms to explain how market linkages contribute to horticultural supply-chain efficiency, offering context-specific evidence from an underexplored horticultural setting.

latest.title: Mapping the evolution of carbon accounting and disclosure research through bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: The intensifying implications of climate change have brought carbon accounting and disclosure to the forefront of policy and scholarly debate, generating an emerging research field that examines its multidimensional nature. Despite the growing body of literature, existing studies remain fragmented and fail to provide a consolidated understanding of the field’s development. This research addresses that gap by conducting a bibliometric examination of 715 Scopus-indexed articles published between 1992 and 2025. Using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer, the study uncovers prominent publication trends, leading authors, and thematic trajectories in carbon accounting research. The results reveal a consistent increase in scholarly output over time, with China identified as the highest contributing nation and journals such as the Journal of Cleaner Production and Sustainability (Switzerland) recognized as the most productive publishing outlets. The most productive author is found to be Professor Tang Q of Western Sydney University. Thematic mapping and co-occurrence analysis highlight six dominant research clusters: Corporate Environmental Disclosure and Performance; Life Cycle and Emission Analysis; Climate Policy and Forest Carbon Sequestration; Technological and Emerging Themes in Carbon Management; Accounting and Methodological Approaches; and Carbon Disclosure, Sustainability, and Regional Empirical Synthesis. This study provides valuable insights into the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of carbon accounting and disclosure research, while offering directions for future inquiry and informing policy discussions in the field.

latest.title: Integrated Assessment Model for Quality and Safety Resources at A Textile Enterprise
latest.abstract: General Background Consistently maintaining product conformity and safety within fabric manufacturing requires the systematic, coordinated governance of personnel, raw materials, equipment, and tracking systems. Specific Background Although ISO 9001 frameworks and defect-control programs are widely utilized, manufacturing facilities traditionally monitor human, material, technological, and informational inputs through disparate and disconnected metrics rather than evaluating their combined systemic status. Knowledge Gap Current literature extensively covers quality governance frameworks and blockchain-based tracking; however, the integrated evaluation of these four interconnected operational dimensions into a single operationalized dynamic index remains unaddressed for fabric enterprises. Aims This study develops and applies a transparent dynamic framework integrating 27 condition proxies across 36 months of operational data to monitor enterprise health and prioritize administrative interventions. Results Utilizing expert-assigned weights for normalization and aggregation, the total overall score demonstrated a marked increase from 0.09 in the first month to 0.97 by month 36. This upward trend indicates measurable improvements across the targeted dimensions—human capital, material inputs, technical stability, and information tracking—providing clear operational, tactical, and strategic decision thresholds for administrators. Novelty This framework introduces a structured, single-metric monitoring scheme combining previously isolated categories, enabling rapid identification of specific operational weaknesses in fabric manufacturing. Implications Plant supervisors can utilize this dynamic index to swiftly detect input deficiencies and target specific interventions, thoug

latest.title: Chuyển đổi số trong doanh nghiệp du lịch vừa và nhỏ: tổng quan hệ thống và đề xuất khung lý thuyết tích hợp
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Chuyển đổi số là xu hướng tất yếu đối với doanh nghiệp du lịch vừa và nhỏ trong bối cảnh cạnh tranh gia tăng sau đại dịch COVID-19. Bài báo tổng quan hệ thống theo quy trình PRISMA 86 nghiên cứu trong nước và quốc tế, chọn lọc từ 379 bản ghi, nhằm hệ thống hóa cơ sở lý thuyết và nhận diện động lực, rào cản, kết quả chuyển đổi số. Trên nền tảng lý thuyết năng lực động, đổi mới mô hình kinh doanh và sức bền tổ chức, nghiên cứu đề xuất khung lý thuyết tích hợp gồm bốn thành phần: bối cảnh và động lực; năng lực số và nguồn lực nội tại; triển khai theo chiều sâu công nghệ; kết quả đa chiều. Ba điểm mới của khung, gồm vai trò điều tiết của năng lực số, ngưỡng năng lực gắn với từng tầng công nghệ và vòng phản hồi từ kết quả về bối cảnh, được cụ thể hóa thành tám mệnh đề có thể kiểm chứng. Bài báo cũng phân tích bảy điều kiện vận dụng khung tại Việt Nam và đề xuất hàm ý cho doanh nghiệp, cơ quan quản lý.

latest.title: The social self in sustainable luxury services: psychological ownership, identification and willingness to use
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on symbolic interactionism, this study aims to examine how social expressiveness influences consumers’ willingness to use sustainable luxury services (SLS). It further investigates the mediating roles of identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being, and the moderating role of psychological ownership. Design/methodology/approach The research uses a two-study design. Study 1 uses survey data from Prolific to test the hypothesized direct, mediation and moderation relationships and to assess the measurement model. Study 2 provides field-based evidence using two Facebook advertisements for a sustainable luxury hotel and click-through rate (CTR) as the behavioral outcome. Study 1 was analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings Social expressiveness is positively associated with willingness to use SLS, and this relationship is sequentially mediated by identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being. Psychological ownership significantly moderates the relationships among social expressiveness, identification, utilitarian well-being and willingness to use SLS; however, the negative interaction terms indicate attenuation rather than the hypothesized strengthening. In Study 2, the social-expressiveness advertisement generated a CTR more than 40% higher than the non-social-expressiveness advertisement. Originality/value This research extends luxury service research by showing how a socially expressive motive is translated into willingness to use SLS through identification and well-being. It also positions psychological ownership as a boundary condition in a non-ownership service context, while showing that high psychological ownership can reduce the marginal importance of other drivers of willingness. The study thereby offe

latest.title: The AI augmentation gap: data richness, automation and business value
latest.abstract: Purpose Grounded in the resource-based view (RBV), this study examines how data richness, as an organisational resource, is associated with business value through two deployment processes, automation and artificial intelligence (AI)-enabled augmentation, and whether they differ in their capacity to generate value. Design/methodology/approach Survey data from 366 Greek firms across four sectors were analysed using partial least squares structural equation modelling (PLS-SEM) with bootstrapped mediation analysis and coefficient-difference tests; business value is measured as perceived value from digital technology. Findings Data richness is positively associated with both deployment processes. Automation is positively associated with business value and channels part of the association between data richness and value, whereas AI-enabled augmentation, the less developed process, shows no significant direct association; the difference is statistically significant, revealing an AI augmentation gap. Data richness also retains a significant direct association with value, and additional analyses suggest that the capability associations with value run through enacted digital transformation. Practical implications Firms should build a strategically governed data foundation, expand automation for near-term returns and develop augmentation as a longer-term capability built on skills, role redesign, validation and trust in AI-supported decisions; EuroMed policy instruments can be aligned with this sequencing. Originality/value Drawing on the RBV, the study shows that deployment processes of the same digital resource differ significantly in their association with value, a heterogeneity interpreted as reflecting the maturity of the complementary capabilities each requires, and provides

latest.title: Impacts of ESG disclosure intensity on trade credit: international evidence
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: This study examines the relationship between ESG disclosure intensity and trade credit using firm-level data from 72 countries over the period 2009–2023. The empirical evidence reveals a U-shaped relationship between ESG disclosure intensity and trade credit. ESG disclosure intensity initially has a negative association with trade credit, but as disclosure intensity increases, its effect becomes more positive for both trade credit received from suppliers and trade credit granted to customers. These findings remain robust across alternative specifications and institutional settings. Among the ESG pillars, environmental and governance disclosures exhibit more pronounced and consistent effects than social disclosures. Overall, this study extends the literature on the nonlinear relationship between ESG disclosure intensity and trade credit and provides a more comprehensive understanding of the implications of ESG disclosure for firms’ trade credit management.

latest.title: Do you really voice for constructiveness? Investigating when and how constructively delivered employee voice fails to be enacted
latest.abstract: Purpose Constructive voice delivery remains a valuable strategy for enhancing managerial voice endorsement. However, its effectiveness may be weakened by how employees present themselves. Drawing on the principle of distinctiveness within attribution theory, this study examines how inconsistencies between employees’ expression of ideas and presentation of strengths influence managerial perceptions and voice endorsement. Design/methodology/approach A multi-source and multi-wave field study was conducted to investigate how employee-exaggerated self-enhancement affects managerial instrumental attribution and subsequent endorsement of constructively delivered voice. Findings The results reveal that employees exhibiting exaggerated self-enhancement are less likely to receive managerial endorsement for their constructively delivered voice, as managers may interpret their voice as instrumental. Originality/value This study highlights that employees’ voice expression and self-presentation are distinct yet interconnected forms of self-expression that shape managerial reactions to employee voice. It offers a more nuanced perspective on how self-expression influences managerial voice endorsement.

latest.title: Smart Kitchen Counter Innovation for Elderly Users Based on Quality Function Deployment and Internet of Things System
latest.venue: ASEAN Journal of Scientific and Technological Reports
authors: Thaya ธยา ภิรมย์ Pirom
latest.abstract: This study aims to design and develop a kitchen counter product for elderly users by applying the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) technique to address user requirements. The study began with a survey of elderly users’ needs, including design, facilities, usability, product quality, and materials. The collected data was analyzed using the QFD product planning matrix and the design deployment matrix to translate customer requirements into technical design specifications. The results indicated that the participants reported a mean perceived satisfaction score of 4.42 out of 5.00 after observing a demonstration of the prototype and its functions in an actual kitchen environment. The five product attributes with the highest satisfaction scores were lighting within overhead cabinet storage compartments, operational safety, ease of maintenance, structural strength, and electrical outlet safety systems, with mean scores of 4.62, 4.57, 4.56, 4.54, and 4.53, respectively. These findings demonstrate that Quality Function Deployment (QFD) is an effective approach for translating user requirements into product design, particularly in the development of kitchen counter products for elderly users. The resulting design was perceived as having the potential to improve safety and convenience for elderly users during kitchen activities. However, further hands-on usability and long-term field testing are required to verify its effectiveness under actual use conditions.

latest.title: Realism or retreat: Unilever weighs the future of purpose
latest.abstract: Research methodology The case was prepared entirely from public secondary sources. These include company regulatory filings submitted to the United States Securities and Exchange Commission, Unilever corporate communications and reporting by established business and trade publications. No primary research was conducted, no interviews were held, and no confidential information was used. No information was disguised. Because the case relies only on public sources and does not draw on privileged access to the protagonists, it does not require a signed protagonist release. All factual claims are attributed in the narrative, and quotations are limited to statements already in the public record. Case overview/synopsis For more than a decade, Unilever was regarded as a leader in purpose led business, built on the Sustainable Living Plan launched under chief executive Paul Polman. In April 2024, under new chief executive Hein Schumacher and amid investor pressure, the company scaled back several environmental and social commitments, including its headline plastics and living wage targets, and narrowed its agenda to four priorities. Schumacher framed the change as realism. Less than a year later he stepped down by mutual agreement, and the former chief financial officer, Fernando Fernandez, took charge and sharpened the reset toward a simpler, more focused portfolio. By 2026, the reset met a condition it had not anticipated, as India, Unilever’s second largest market, converted recycled content from ambition into binding law just as the parent company loosened its voluntary targets, leaving Fernandez to set commitments for the next reporting cycle. The case places students at that decision and asks whether a firm’s social and environmental commitments are a defensive strategic a

latest.title: Copy, paste, and obfuscate? Readability and standardisation in integrated reporting
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting in Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This study examines how readability and textual similarity evolve and interact in integrated reports, investigating whether narrative accessibility and textual standardisation are distinct characteristics or interconnected features of institutionalised reporting practices. Design/methodology/approach A longitudinal panel of 1,393 firm-year observations from South African listed companies over 2015–2024 is analysed. Readability is measured using Flesch Reading Ease, and textual similarity using cosine similarity between consecutive reports. Fixed-effects panel regressions are supplemented by governance-excluded similarity measures, first-difference models, persistence analysis and an alternative readability measure. Findings Readability declines over time, while textual similarity remains high, with no consistent upward trend. Textual similarity is positively associated with readability, indicating that narrative continuity can coexist with greater accessibility. However, this association becomes insignificant when governance-related disclosures are excluded, suggesting that it is concentrated within a highly institutionalised disclosure domain characterised by recurring reporting requirements and stable narrative structures. Additional analyses confirm the persistence of textual similarity and robustness of the main findings. Originality/value This study extends research that has largely examined readability and textual similarity separately by demonstrating that these characteristics are interrelated and that their association depends on the disclosure domain. Greater readability can coexist with substantial textual standardisation, complicating the interpretation of this as an unambiguous indicator of disclosure quality or transparency. latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Private sustainability engagement in an emerging economy
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting in Emerging Economies
latest.abstract: Purpose This study critically examines how private sustainability engagement functions as a form of dialogic accountability when Nordic institutional investors interact with publicly listed companies in a state-dominated emerging economy, challenging the implicit universalism of consensus-seeking engagement models. Design/methodology/approach The study employs qualitative content analysis of Nordic investor engagement reports documenting extended interactions with Egyptian financial and telecommunication companies. Legitimacy theory, neo-institutional theory and dialogic accountability provide an integrated lens for examining information exchange and corporate answerability. Findings Private engagements centre on political connections and human rights risks, with documented response patterns consistent with a prioritisation of political licence to operate over substantive answerability to international investors. The documented engagements record evidential burdens preventing independent verification. The response patterns across both cases constitute dialogic deadlock – a structural ceiling where genuine accountability exchange is foreclosed. Originality/value Empirically, the study provides an in-depth qualitative content analysis of investor-side engagement reports, documenting the sustainability information Nordic investors seek in two Egyptian private engagements and the patterns of corporate response. Theoretically, it proposes political licence and audience primacy as concepts for interpreting the documented exchanges and specifies the contextual conditions under which audience hierarchy may shift toward audience primacy. Conceptually, it theorises dialogic deadlock as a structural outcome arising where legitimacy incentives prove insufficient and the preconditio

latest.title: Assessing the impact of gender affirming endocrine interventions on the mental health and well-being among transgender youth
latest.abstract: Purpose In the absence of previous systematic longitudinal evidence, this pilot study aims to evaluate the quality of life (QOL) of transgender youth in relation to several other psychological variables impacting the mental health of youth. Design/methodology/approach The cross-sectional descriptive study, conducted as a small-scale trial run, examined several mental health variables such as stress, anxiety, depression, social support, resilience and self-efficacy influencing the QOL of the transgender youth. The participants were assessed for relevant, detailed demographic and clinical information, along with a semi-structured questionnaire. Findings The pilot study included 50 transgenders between 18 and 25 years age category, categorized as youth. Descriptive data indicated the diversity in the demography and perception of transgender individuals about the gender-affirming care received during transitions. The favorable scores of Cronbach’s alpha indicated that the tool is highly reliable for measuring the intended objectives. Low scores of depression, anxiety and stress indicate a good QOL among the youth. Further results also indicate that the gender affirmation care received has a greater impact on the mental health variables that determine the self-identity of the trans individuals. Originality/value Mental health plays a critical role in determining the QOL of transgenders. Therefore, studying the longitudinal impact on suitable gender-affirming endocrine interventions can provide a foundation for drawing evidence-based health care practices and policies to protect the transgender youth, thereby promoting their effective functioning in the society.

latest.title: Tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng của người tiêu dùng trẻ trong mua sắm livestream: bằng chứng từ ngành thời trang Việt Nam
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Trong lĩnh vực livestream thời trang tại Việt Nam, hành vi ra quyết định mua của nhóm khách hàng trẻ chịu ảnh hưởng bởi các tín hiệu xã hội, đặc biệt là cảm giác sợ bỏ lỡ và xu hướng hành động theo đám đông. Dựa trên khung Kích thích – Chủ thể – Phản hồi (S-O-R), nghiên cứu kiểm định tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ (FoMO) và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng, đồng thời phân tích vai trò trung gian của trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng. Dữ liệu 308 người tiêu dùng trẻ đã tham gia mua sắm livestream thời trang được phân tích bằng PLS-SEM. Kết quả cho thấy, FoMO và hiệu ứng đám đông đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng và hành vi mua bốc đồng. Trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng đóng vai trò trung gian một phần. Nghiên cứu góp phần cung cấp thêm bằng chứng thực nghiệm trong livestream commerce ngành thời trang tại Việt Nam và gợi ý hàm ý quản trị cho doanh nghiệp.

latest.title: Fostering Innovative Work Behaviour Through Positive Work Environment: The Moderating Role of Ambidextrous Leadership Evidence From Structural Equation Modeling Approach
latest.abstract: Innovation is increasingly recognised as a critical driver of organizational competitiveness, yet the mechanisms that foster employees’ innovative work behaviour (IWB) remain underexplored. This study investigates the effect of a positive work environment on IWB, with a focus on the moderating role of ambidextrous leadership. Drawing on organizational climate and leadership theories, the research proposes that supportive workplace conditions directly encourage creativity and idea generation, while ambidextrous leadership balancing opening behaviours that promote exploration with closing behaviours that ensure discipline enhances the translation of these ideas into actionable innovations. A quantitative, cross-sectional survey design was employed, with data collected from industry professionals using validated scales for workplace climate, ambidextrous leadership, and innovative work behaviour. Structural Equation Modeling (SEM) was applied to test the hypothesized relationships. The findings are expected to confirm that positive work environments significantly influence IWB, and that ambidextrous leadership moderates this relationship, thereby strengthening the impact of workplace positivity on innovation outcomes. This study contributes theoretically by bridging organizational climate and leadership research, extending ambidextrous leadership theory to individual-level innovation, and clarifying pathways to innovation. Practically, it offers actionable insights for organizations to cultivate supportive environments and develop ambidextrous leadership capabilities, ensuring sustained innovation in dynamic markets.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: Relocation of the Fuel Fast Fill Unit on the Komatsu PC2000 from Beneath the Engine to the Unit Stairs as an Effort to Improve Safety, Refueling Efficiency, and Reduce Production Loss Time (Case Study of Quality Control Project Implementation in the AMM Pit Area, Mifa Jobsite, PT Putra Perkasa Abadi, 2025)
latest.abstract: The Komatsu PC2000 excavator operating in the AMM Pit Area at the Mifa Jobsite was equipped with a fast-fill fuel system positioned beneath the engine, exposing its components to potential damage from boulder impacts and creating accessibility challenges during refueling operations. Maintenance records from February 2024 to July 2025 documented nine system-related incidents resulting in at least 25 hours of equipment downtime, of which 16.7 hours (66.8%) were attributed to structural damage. This study evaluated the relocation of the fast-fill fuel connection point from beneath the engine to the excavator stairway area using the eight-step Quality Control Circle (QCC) methodology integrated with the Plan–Do–Check–Act (PDCA) cycle. Data were collected through maintenance records, field observations, cross-functional team discussions, Pareto analysis, Ishikawa cause-and-effect analysis, and solution-selection matrices to identify the primary causes of equipment downtime and determine appropriate corrective measures. Following the relocation, no additional fast-fill system disturbances were recorded during the specified monitoring period. For seven Komatsu PC2000 excavators, the projected operational benefits included annual savings of 638.5 equipment operating hours, a reduction in fuel consumption of approximately 76,620 liters, and a potential productivity gain of 447,125 bank cubic meters (BCM). However, these estimates were based on projected operational scenarios rather than independently verified annual performance measurements. The reported implementation cost was IDR 34,815,899 per excavator. Overall, the modification improved access to the refueling connection and potentially reduced component exposure to mechanical impacts, although its long-term reliability, sa

latest.title: Pet insurance services adoption: how values, reasoning, and insurance literacy shape consumer intentions in an emerging market
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine pet-insurance adoption in India through behavioral reasoning theory (BRT), focusing on how openness to change and social value shape reasons for and against adoption, how these reasons influence attitude and purchase intention and whether insurance literacy strengthens the attitude–intention relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Interviews with 17 pet owners identified the facilitators and inhibitors. Survey data from 352 respondents were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the mediation and moderation effects. Demographic moderation was treated as an exploratory analysis. Findings Openness to change strengthened both reasons for and reasons against adoption, whereas social value strengthened supportive reasoning and reduced opposing reasoning. Reasons for adoption positively influenced attitude and intention, whereas reasons against adoption had negative effects. Attitude was the strongest predictor of purchase intention, and insurance literacy strengthened the attitude–intention relationship. The unexpected positive association between openness to change and reasons against adoption suggests that receptiveness to novelty may intensify scrutiny of benefits and barriers instead of uniformly increasing adoption readiness. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional sample limits the causal inference and generalizability of the findings. Future research should test the deliberative role of openness to change using longitudinal, behavioral and cross-market designs. Practical implications Insurers should address benefits and barriers, including affordability, exclusions, coverage limits and claims procedures, while using pet-insurance education

latest.title: Changes in Anxiety Scores After Butterfly Hug Sessions Among Grade XII Students in Banjar
latest.abstract: Introduction: Brief relaxation activities may support adolescent wellbeing, but evidence for butterfly hug in schools remains limited. Objective: To examine changes in anxiety questionnaire scores before and after butterfly hug sessions among Grade XII students at SMA Negeri 1 Banjar. Method: This exploratory one-group pretest-posttest study included 40 students aged 17–18 years selected from 81 screened students. Anxiety was assessed using an electronic self-report HARS adaptation without established adolescent validity. Six 15-minute sessions with music and breathing were delivered three times weekly on April 10-22, 2026; attendance was 100%. Posttest was on April 23. The paired t test was supplemented by Shapiro–Wilk and Wilcoxon analyses of reconstructed pairs. Result: Mean anxiety scores decreased from 18.15 to 16.00, with a mean reduction of 2.15 points (95% CI: 1.338–2.962; p < 0.001). After the intervention, most students were classified as having mild anxiety (80%), while the proportion with moderate anxiety decreased from 45% to 20%. Conclusion: Following six butterfly hug sessions accompanied by breathing exercises and music over two weeks, 40 Grade XII students at SMA Negeri 1 Banjar showed a decrease in mean anxiety scores from 18.15 to 16.00, representing a reduction of 2.15 points. The paired-samples t test indicated a statistically significant difference (p < 0.001). The proportion of students with moderate anxiety decreased from 45% to 20%, while the proportion with mild anxiety increased from 55% to 80%. These findings provide preliminary support for further evaluation of butterfly hug as a supportive activity for anxiety management in schools.

latest.title: The Influence of Training and Development, Education and Learning, Performance Management, and Career Development on Nurses' Performance
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze the effect of Training and Development, Education and Learning, Performance Management, and Career Development on nurse performance in the Hemodialysis Unit of Ratu Aji Putri Botung Regional Hospital, North Penajam Paser Regency. The study used a quantitative design with a survey approach, supplemented by qualitative data to obtain a comprehensive understanding. Quantitative data were collected through a Likert-scale questionnaire from the entire population of 31 nurses, while qualitative data were obtained through semi-structured interviews and documentation studies. Data analysis was conducted using descriptive analysis and multiple linear regression to test the partial and simultaneous effects of independent variables on nurse performance. The results showed that partially, Training and Development, Education and Learning, and Career Development did not significantly influence nurse performance. Conversely, Performance Management significantly influenced nurse performance. However, simultaneously, all four human resource development variables significantly influenced nurse performance. These findings indicate that in standardized, high-risk clinical work units such as hemodialysis, an objective performance management system, regular evaluations, and consistent feedback are dominant factors in improving performance. Meanwhile, individual development factors serve more as supporting factors that contribute collectively. This study recommends strengthening the performance management system integrated with human resource development programs and adjusting development policies based on the characteristics of the work unit.

hot.title: Trust in scientists and their role in society across 68 countries
hot.abstract: Science is crucial for evidence-based decision-making. Public trust in scientists can help decision makers act on the basis of the best available evidence, especially during crises. However, in recent years the epistemic authority of science has been challenged, causing concerns about low public trust in scientists. We interrogated these concerns with a preregistered 68-country survey of 71,922 respondents and found that in most countries, most people trust scientists and agree that scientists should engage more in society and policymaking. We found variations between and within countries, which we explain with individual- and country-level variables, including political orientation. While there is no widespread lack of trust in scientists, we cannot discount the concern that lack of trust in scientists by even a small minority may affect considerations of scientific evidence in policymaking. These findings have implications for scientists and policymakers seeking to maintain and increase trust in scientists.

hot.title: Interaction with AI companions and psychological well-being
How generative AI Is shaping the future of marketing
hot.venue: Journal of the Academy of Marketing Science
hot.abstract: Abstract Generative AI (Gen AI) is shaping the future of marketing. In the next decade, Gen AI will influence how marketers interact and communicate with customers, help create and deliver marketing content (text, images, and video), and inform methods for researching and developing new products and services. In both service and sales settings, Gen AI will affect customers directly and significantly. Therefore, marketers, researchers, and public policy makers require a clear understanding of Gen AI and its potential, as well as its limitations. To assist marketers in thinking through the adoption and implementation of Gen AI, the current article presents a four-quadrant organizing framework that highlights trade-offs in both the nature of Gen AI inputs and the extent of human augmentation needed to deliver Gen AI–generated outputs. This framework provides guidance for the selection and implementation of Gen AI tools, as well as recommendations for further research.

hot.title: The evolving field of digital mental health: current evidence and implementation issues for smartphone apps, generative artificial intelligence, and virtual reality
hot.abstract: The expanding domain of digital mental health is transitioning beyond traditional telehealth to incorporate smartphone apps, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence, including large language models. While industry setbacks and methodological critiques have highlighted gaps in evidence and challenges in scaling these technologies, emerging solutions rooted in co-design, rigorous evaluation, and implementation science offer promising pathways forward. This paper underscores the dual necessity of advancing the scientific foundations of digital mental health and increasing its real-world applicability through five themes. First, we discuss recent technological advances in digital phenotyping, virtual reality, and generative artificial intelligence. Progress in this latter area, specifically designed to create new outputs such as conversations and images, holds unique potential for the mental health field. Given the spread of smartphone apps, we then evaluate the evidence supporting their utility across various mental health contexts, including well-being, depression, anxiety, schizophrenia, eating disorders, and substance use disorders. This broad view of the field highlights the need for a new generation of more rigorous, placebo-controlled, and real-world studies. We subsequently explore engagement challenges that hamper all digital mental health tools, and propose solutions, including human support, digital navigators, just-in-time adaptive interventions, and personalized approaches. We then analyze implementation issues, emphasizing clinician engagement, service integration, and scalable delivery models. hot.title: Artificial Intelligence and Its Role in Shaping Organizational Work Practices and Culture
hot.abstract: The advent of Artificial Intelligence (AI) is profoundly transforming organizational landscapes, significantly influencing work practices and triggering cultural shifts. This study explores the role of AI in reshaping organizational work practices and examines the resulting cultural transformation. Through a systematic literature review, this study synthesizes existing research to provide a comprehensive understanding of AI’s impact on organizational landscapes. A systematic literature review was conducted, analyzing peer-reviewed articles, books, and conference papers to identify key themes related to AI-driven changes in work practices, including automation, decision making, and employee roles. It also explores how these changes influence organizational culture, particularly shifts toward innovation, agility, and continuous learning, alongside challenges like resistance to change and ethical concerns. While AI adoption promises benefits such as enhanced efficiency, productivity, and innovation, it also presents significant challenges related to cultural alignment, employee resistance, ethical concerns, and leadership communication. Effective leadership, transparent communication, and investments in skills development emerge as pivotal strategies for overcoming these obstacles and ensuring successful AI implementation. The findings offer insights into the complex interplay between AI adoption and cultural transformation, highlighting gaps in the current research and suggesting directions for future studies. This study serves as a valuable resource for academics and practitioners seeking to understand the broader implications of AI on organizational structures and culture.

hot.title: Job demands-resources and conservation of resources theories: How do they help to explain employee well-being and future job design?
hot.abstract: This paper examines the Conservation of Resources (COR) theory and the Job Demands-Resources (JD-R) theory to understand and predict employee well-being and performance. COR theory suggests that individuals aim to acquire, protect, and maximize resources to reduce psychological distress and prevent burnout. JD-R theory posits that balancing job demands and resources affects employee well-being, behaviors, and performance. By exploring these theories together, the paper offers insights into supporting the workforce amid challenges like remote work and technological advancements. It highlights shared features and differences between the theories, unresolved issues, and research opportunities, such as operationalizing and testing COR theory and differentiating job demands and resources in JD-R theory. The paper concludes with predictions about future job design, emphasizing the need to balance job demands and resources to support employee well-being and performance, contributing to the literature by challenging and refining these theories.

hot.title: Sustainable Consumption and Branding for Gen Z: How Brand Dimensions Influence Consumer Behavior and Adoption of Newly Launched Technological Products
hot.abstract: Generation Z is emerging as a powerful force in shaping global consumer behavior, particularly in the market of digital and technological products. This study examines how specific branding dimensions, such as online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and brand knowledge, influence Gen Z’s purchase intention, emphasizing sustainable consumption. Sustainable consumption, in this context, refers to the preference for tech products that minimize the environmental impact through eco-friendly design, energy efficiency, and responsible sourcing. Using a quantitative approach, this cross-sectional research explores the effects of online brand experience, engagement, image, trust, loyalty, awareness, behavioral intention, and knowledge on purchasing newly launched technological products that align with sustainability. Data were collected from a Gen Z sample using a combination of convenience and systematic sampling, and multiple regression analysis identified the most significant predictors of purchase intention. The results indicate that online brand experience, brand image, brand trust, and brand loyalty play the most crucial roles, having a greater effects on Gen Z’s purchase intention, while brand awareness and knowledge also contribute. However, brand engagement and behavioral intention have weaker effects. These findings suggest that brands targeting Gen Z should prioritize building a strong, trustworthy, and engaging online presence while highlighting their sustainability efforts, and when Gen Z consumers have favorable digital interactions with a brand, perceive its image positively, trust it, and feel loyal to it, they are more likely to consider purchasing its sustainable offerings. This study enhances the understandi

hot.title: The impact of artificial intelligence on organizational performance: The mediating role of employee productivity
hot.venue: Journal of Open Innovation Technology Market and Complexity
hot.abstract: The adoption of Artificial intelligence (AI) technology in the workplace is becoming more common, with several research highlighting both its positive and adverse influence on employee productivity (EP) and organizational performance (OP). Furthermore, there is a scarcity of research focused on the mediator role of EP in the nexus between AI and OP. This ambiguity underscores the need for a comprehensive understanding of how AI interacts with EP and OP within specific organizational contexts, such as Ethio Telecom. Therefore, this study aimed to investigate the impact of AI on OP with a mediating role of EP. Quantitative data was collected through an online survey using Kobo Toolbox from 172 purposively selected employees. AI was modeled as third-order formative construct, while EP and OP were first-order reflective constructs. The variables were measured using validated multi-item questionnaires with a 7-point Likert scale. The association between these variables was investigated with PLS-SEM in SMART PLS 4.1.03. The results showed that there were positive and significant relationships between AI and EP, AI and OP, EP and OP, and AI on OP through EP. Furthermore, EP served as a partial mediator between OP and AI. These findings are consistent with previous studies and theories, such as the resource-based view and human capital theories. The results suggest that organizations can dramatically improve performance in the digital age by implementing AI and creating a work environment that encourages productivity.

hot.title: The moderating role of personalized recommendations in the trust–satisfaction–loyalty relationship: an empirical study of AI-driven e-commerce
hot.abstract: Abstract Purpose This study investigates the effects of trust, satisfaction, and loyalty on AI-driven e-commerce, with a particular focus on how personalized recommendations moderate these relationships. It aims to explore how personalized AI features reshape consumer perceptions and decision-making. Design/methodology/approach A quantitative research approach was used to collect data from a diverse group of e-commerce users who had interacted with AI-based recommendation systems. An online survey employing standardized scales for trust, satisfaction, loyalty, and personalization was administered, and data were analyzed using structural equation modeling (SEM) to test the hypotheses. Findings The study reveals that trust has a significant positive influence on both satisfaction and loyalty. Personalization further strengthens these relationships by moderating the trust–satisfaction–loyalty dynamic. Satisfaction partially mediates the relationship between trust and loyalty, with the model’s explanatory power improving by 5% when personalization is included as a moderator. These results highlight the pivotal role of personalized recommendations in shaping consumer trust and satisfaction in AI-driven e-commerce. Practical implications Businesses can use personalized recommendation systems to enhance trust and satisfaction, thereby fostering loyalty. For example, platforms like Amazon and Netflix have successfully employed personalized AI algorithms to boost customer retention and engagement. Transparency features, such as explaining why certain products are recommended, and cultural sensitivity in algorithm design can further enhance customer trust and acceptance. e-commerce organizations should also invest in data privacy measures and clear algorithms to maintain consumer

hot.title: A Closer Look into Recent Video-based Learning Research: A Comprehensive Review of Video Characteristics, Tools, Technologies, and Learning Effectiveness
hot.venue: International Journal of Artificial Intelligence in Education
hot.abstract: People increasingly use videos on the Web for learning, be it for daily tasks in formal or informal educational settings. To enhance this type of learning, scientists are continuously conducting experiments, proposing guidelines, analyzing data, and researching artificial intelligence methods for tool development. In this comprehensive review, we analyze 257 articles (using PRISMA guidelines) on video-based learning from a technological perspective for the period from 2016 to 2021. One of the aims is to identify video characteristics that support learning as explored by previous research. Based on our analysis, we suggest a taxonomy that organizes the video characteristics and contextual aspects into eight categories: (1) audio features, (2) visual features, (3) textual features, (4) instructor behavior, (5) learners’ activities (play, pause, etc.), (6) interactive features (quizzes, etc.), (7) production style, and (8) instructional design. Also, we identify four representative methodological approaches: (1) tool support of video-based learning, (2) controlled experiments, (3) data analysis studies, and (4) design guidelines for learning videos. We find that the most explored characteristics are textual features followed by visual features, learners’ activities, and interactive features. Tools that aid learning through videos frequently utilize text from transcripts, video frames, and images. The learner’s activity is heavily explored through log files in data analysis studies, and interactive features are frequently scrutinized in controlled experiments. As further contributions, we contrast research findings on how video characteristics affect learning effectiveness, report on tasks and technologies used to develop tools, and summarize design guideline trends to prod

hot.title: Building trust in sustainable brands: Revisiting perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image
hot.abstract: This study revisits the key variables that build brand trust in consumers, addressing a critical issue for building lasting relationships between brands and consumers. Through a conceptual model, we examine how perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image influence consumer trust. The research is based on a sample of 1280 Spanish consumers over the age of 18, who responded to a questionnaire designed with previously validated scales. The PLS-SEM technique was used to validate the hypotheses and the proposed model. The findings reveal that perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image have a positive and significant effect on consumer trust. In particular, it was found that customer service directly influences customer satisfaction, which in turn reinforces brand trust. Additionally, the brand's communication strategy shows a significant positive relationship with brand image. Finally, customer satisfaction is identified as a mediating variable in the relationship between customer service and trust, indicating that a positive experience with customer service is fundamental for consolidating brand trust. This study contributes to enhancing the understanding of the factors that promote brand trust and offers practical implications for the development of effective marketing and brand management strategies. These insights can be especially relevant for sustainable brands, as the identified factors—perceived value, satisfaction, customer service, and brand image—are also critical in fostering trust in brands that prioritize sustainability. Incorporating sustainable practices into these areas may further strengthen consumer trust and loyalty toward sustainable brands.

hot.title: Leading in the Digital Age: The Role of Leadership in Organizational Digital Transformation
hot.abstract: In the modern digital age, organizations face unprecedented challenges and possibilities while managing the intricacies of digital transformation. Accelerated technological developments, changing customer preferences, heightened competition, and dynamic regulatory environments necessitate companies to synchronize their business goals with technological innovations. Leadership is crucial in steering businesses through changes, requiring a deep understanding of change processes and the capacity to adjust leadership accordingly. This research addresses the central question: How does leadership effectively promote organizational digital transformation? The study examines how leaders can effectively promote the adoption of advanced technologies and the promotion of innovation, by first exploring the nature of digital transformation within organizations and then analyzing the evolving dynamics of leadership in this context. An integrative review of the Web of Science (WoS) and Scopus databases was conducted, using the search terms: “Leadership” and “Digital Transformation”. The findings emphasize that effective leadership is crucial for managing the minutiae of digital transformation, integrating technology into organizational processes to facilitate learning, collaboration, and agility, enabling companies to adapt to market shifts, reduce uncertainty, and enhance decision-making for sustainable growth. By using the right tools and with the right frequency, leaders may develop team cohesion—even at a distance. Attentive digital-age leaders will know how to leverage the right mechanisms, and herein, we hope to give some indication of how that may be achieved, so that digital transformation increases rather than decreases team motivation levels.

hot.title: Why human–AI relationships need socioaffective alignment
hot.abstract: Humans strive to design safe AI systems that align with our goals and remain under our control. However, as AI capabilities advance, we face a new challenge: the emergence of deeper, more persistent relationships between humans and AI systems. We explore how increasingly capable AI agents may generate the perception of deeper relationships with users, especially as AI becomes more personalised and agentic. This shift, from transactional interaction to ongoing sustained social engagement with AI, necessitates a new focus on socioaffective alignment—how an AI system behaves within the social and psychological ecosystem co-created with its user, where preferences and perceptions evolve through mutual influence. Addressing these dynamics involves resolving key intrapersonal dilemmas, including balancing immediate versus long-term well-being, protecting autonomy, and managing AI companionship alongside the desire to preserve human social bonds. By framing these challenges through a notion of basic psychological needs, we seek AI systems that support, rather than exploit, our fundamental nature as social and emotional beings.

hot.title: Greenwashing prevention in environmental, social, and governance (ESG) disclosures: A bibliometric analysis
hot.venue: Research in International Business and Finance
hot.abstract: The accuracy and reliability of environmental, social, and governance (hereafter ESG) reporting are threatened by the presence of greenwashing which affects the quality of disclosure, complicates the decision-making process, adversely influences financial markets, and affects stakeholders’ trust in disclosed information. This study examines the academic literature on ESG disclosure and greenwashing prevention through a bibliometric analysis and systematic literature review. Our findings show that greenwashing is a complex phenomenon characterised by various forms, shapes, and levels, making it challenging to detect, measure, and develop prevention tools. The results show a growing trend in the academic literature on greenwashing with a strong focus on the establishment of greenwashing detection measures and the need for the creation of greenwashing prevention tools to ensure the reliability, comparability, and quality of corporate sustainability reporting. Understanding the challenges of greenwashing in ESG disclosures and the efforts toward greenwashing prevention carries significant implications for regulators and standard-setters, supervisory bodies, professional organizations, companies, researchers, and other stakeholders, especially in light of recent regulatory developments around the globe and the new forms and levels of greenwashing evolving in scientific research. • Greenwashing prevention in ESG disclosures analysed through a bibliometric analysis. • Performance, network, and systematic literature review analysis methods applied. • Greenwashing measurement is difficult as it has lots of levels, forms, and shades. • Greenwashing measurement methods at various greenwashing levels are systemized. • The creation of a credible greenwashing prevention tool in ESG d

hot.title: AI and employee wellbeing in the workplace: An empirical study
hot.abstract: The integration of artificial intelligence (AI) in workplace settings significantly affects employees, particularly their wellbeing. Despite its growing relevance, the impact of AI on employee wellbeing remains underexplored. To address this gap, we conducted a survey and employed structural equation modeling to analyze data from Finnish and international companies headquartered in Finland (n = 207). We found that AI adoption does not directly impact employee wellbeing but indirectly influences it through work-related factors of task optimization and safety. This highlights the importance of strategically implementing AI to enhance aspects of work that are important to employees, thereby maximizing the wellbeing benefits of AI adoption. Practically, this study underscores the need for AI adoption to result in tangible improvements in organizational tasks and processes, data security, and occupational health. When these aspects are adequately addressed, AI adoption can enhance employee wellbeing and contribute to improved human-AI integration in the workplace.

hot.title: The Typing Cure: Experiences with Large Language Model Chatbots for Mental Health Support
hot.venue: Proceedings of the ACM on Human-Computer Interaction
hot.abstract: People experiencing severe distress increasingly use Large Language Model (LLM) chatbots as mental health support tools. Discussions on social media have described how engagements were lifesaving for some, but evidence suggests that general-purpose LLM chatbots also have notable risks that could endanger the welfare of users if not designed responsibly. In this study, we investigate the lived experiences of people who have used LLM chatbots for mental health support. We build on interviews with 21 individuals from globally diverse backgrounds to analyze how users create unique support roles for their chatbots, fill in gaps in everyday care, and navigate associated cultural limitations when seeking support from chatbots. We ground our analysis in psychotherapy literature around effective support, and introduce the concept of therapeutic alignment, or aligning AI with therapeutic values for mental health contexts. Our study offers recommendations for how designers can approach the ethical and effective use of LLM chatbots and other AI mental health support tools in mental health care.

hot.title: Confronting and alleviating AI resistance in the workplace: An integrative review and a process framework
hot.abstract: This study involves an integrative literature review and a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee Artificial intelligence (AI) resistance in organizations. First, we conceptualize AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. We advance that experiencing mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection are key individual mechanisms to confronting AI resistance connected to organizational mechanisms to alleviate AI resistance through the continuous interaction and unfolding of anxiety and introspection. We also explain the alleviation of AI resistance as an organizational process consisting of AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation, each of which maps into one of the dimensions in the employee-level confrontation mechanisms. Overall, our conceptual framework provides an overarching and granular understanding of AI resistance, how employees confront it, and how it can be alleviated in the workplace. • Develops a process framework explaining the mechanisms to confront and alleviate employee AI resistance. • AI resistance as a three-dimensional concept embodied in employees' fears, inefficacies, and antipathies toward AI. • Highlights mistrust, existential questioning, and technological reflection as key individual concerns • AI resistance is alleviated through AI accessibility, human-AI augmentation, and AI-technology legitimation.

hot.title: Gamification in education and training: A literature review
hot.abstract: Abstract Gamification, when properly implemented in education and training, can increase the engagement and motivation of learners and inspire them to change aspects of their behaviour to support learning. Although the use of gamification in the learning process might have a positive impact, its potential to strengthen education and training has not yet been confirmed. The descriptive literature review presented in this article synthesises studies and findings on the use of gamification in the education and training context. The authors used the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic Reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) model to select and analyse 46 publications from six bibliographic databases. They investigated the gamification theories, frameworks, models, elements and mechanics that can support learning. In addition, research was conducted to identify constraints, challenges and organisational impediments that may arise in gamified education and training programmes, to answer the question of how gamification can be implemented to achieve better learning outcomes. Findings show that further studies need to be conducted into this evolving learning approach. Overall, gamification is most likely to be effective when instructional design principles are used to ensure training content meets learners’ needs and expectations.

hot.title: Insights from the Job Demands–Resources Model: AI's dual impact on employees’ work and life well-being
hot.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) has rapidly integrated into organizational workflows, sparking two debates: proponents argue that it increases productivity and decreases workloads, whereas opponents warn that it induces technostress (e.g., job replacement) and decreases employees' well-being. However, AI adoption by employees remains understudied, requiring both theoretical and empirical investigation to assess its positive and negative effects. This study employs the job demands–resources (JD–R) model as a guiding framework to examine the impact of AI demands (i.e., technostress) and resources (i.e., efficacy and generative AI) on employees' work and life domains (i.e., productivity, job satisfaction, and work–family conflict), with engagement and exhaustion as mediating factors. Data gathering through a three-wave survey involved 600 gender-balanced participants working with AI across diverse industries. Bayesian SEM results indicate that both AI efficacy and generative AI positively impact productivity, with AI efficacy also enhancing engagement and job satisfaction. In contrast, AI technostress increases exhaustion, exacerbates work–family conflict, and lowers job satisfaction, even though it may still contribute to productivity. These findings highlight the dual impact of AI on employees: AI technostress impairs well-being, while AI efficacy enhances it. Notably, generative AI mitigates the negative effects of technostress, a benefit not observed for AI efficacy as measured in this study. Overall, this study provides an empirical basis for understanding the resources and demands associated with AI adoption and its impact on employees' psychological processes, influencing both their work and life domains and leading to diverse outcomes. • This study explores how AI at

The Global Flourishing Study: Study Profile and Initial Results on Flourishing
hot.abstract: The Global Flourishing Study is a longitudinal panel study of over 200,000 participants in 22 geographically and culturally diverse countries, spanning all six populated continents, with nationally representative sampling and intended annual survey data collection for 5 years to assess numerous aspects of flourishing and its possible determinants. The study is intended to expand our knowledge of the distribution and determinants of flourishing around the world. Relations between a composite flourishing index and numerous demographic characteristics are reported. Participants were also surveyed about their childhood experiences, which were analyzed to determine their associations with subsequent adult flourishing. Analyses are presented both across and within countries, and discussion is given as to how the demographic and childhood relationships vary by country and which patterns appear to be universal versus culturally specific. Brief comment is also given on the results of a whole series of papers in the Global Flourishing Study Special Collection, employing similar analyses, but with more-specific aspects of well-being. The Global Flourishing Study expands our knowledge of the distribution and determinants of well-being and provides foundational knowledge for the promotion of societal flourishing.

hot.title: Global, regional, and national burden of suicide, 1990–2021: a systematic analysis for the Global Burden of Disease Study 2021
hot.abstract: BACKGROUND: Deaths from suicide are a tragic yet preventable cause of mortality. Quantifying the burden of suicide to understand its geographical distribution, temporal trends, and variation by age and sex is an essential step in suicide prevention. We aimed to present a comprehensive set of global, regional, and national estimates of suicide burden. METHODS: We produced estimates of the number of deaths and age-standardised mortality rates of suicide globally, regionally, and for 204 countries and territories from 1990 to 2021, and disaggregated these results by age and sex. The Global Burden of Diseases, Injuries, and Risk Factors Study (GBD) 2021 estimates of deaths attributable to suicide were broken down into two comprehensive categories: those by firearms and those by other specified means. For this analysis, we also produced estimates of mean age at the time of death from suicide, incidence of suicide attempts compared with deaths, and age-standardised rates of suicide by firearm. We acquired data from vital registration, verbal autopsy, and mortality surveillance that included 23 782 study-location-years of data from GBD 2021. Point estimates were calculated from the average of 1000 randomly selected possible values of deaths from suicide by age, sex, and geographical location. 95% uncertainty intervals (UIs) were derived from the 2·5th and 97·5th percentiles from a 1000-draw distribution. FINDINGS: Globally, 746 000 deaths (95% UI 692 000-800 000) from suicide occurred in 2021, including 519 000 deaths (485 000-556 000) among males and 227 000 (200 000-255 000) among females.
