hot.title: Collaborative AI in the workplace: Enhancing organizational performance through resource-based and task-technology fit perspectives
hot.abstract: This research examines how artificial intelligence, human capabilities, and task types influence organizational outcomes. By leveraging the frameworks of the Resource-Based View and Task Technology Fit theories, we executed two distinct studies to assess the effectiveness of a generative AI tool in aiding task performance across a spectrum of task complexities and creative demands. The initial study tested the utility of generative AI across diverse tasks and the significance of AI-related skills enhancement. The subsequent study explored interactions between humans and AI, analyzing emotional tone, sentence structure, and word choice. Our results indicate that incorporating AI can significantly improve organizational task performance in areas such as automation, support, creative endeavors, and innovation processes. We also observed that generative AI generally presents more positive sentiment, utilizes simpler language, and has a narrower vocabulary than human counterparts. These insights contribute to a broader understanding of AI's strengths and weaknesses in organizational settings and guide the strategic implementation of AI systems. • Firms can utilize AI to gain competitive advantages. • Firms can deploy AI to automate routine tasks and enhance decision support tasks. • Firms should focus on AI and human collaboration to boost creative and innovative tasks. • Firms benefit when employees upskill to improve performance with AI. • Generative AI tool in our study had a more positive sentiment and used simpler language than humans.

hot.title: The impacts of companion AI on human relationships: risks, benefits, and design considerations
hot.abstract: AI applications intended for companionship have increased in both availability and capabilities in recent years, alongside a spike in loneliness (Johnson 2023 ; Murthy 2023 ). According to a 2024 analysis by venture capital firm Andreessen Horowitz, companion AI makes up 16 of the top 100 AI apps based on web traffic and monthly active users (Moore 2024 ). Moreover, today’s AI applications have a greater command of human language, an increasing capacity for storing memories, and more varied modalities to support an increasing diversity of experiences, a known driver in the development and deepening of emotional relationships (Skjuve et al. 2022 ).

hot.title: Organizational culture, digital transformation, and product innovation
hot.abstract: This research fills a knowledge gap by introducing a new conceptualization of digital transformation through a multidimensional digital transforming capability. It further examines the influence of four cultural types on this capability and its subsequent impact on product innovation . Empirical findings reveal that adhocracy, followed in descending order of influence by clan, market, and hierarchy cultures, is positively related to digital transforming capability, which in turn is positively related to product innovation in terms of new product newness, meaningfulness, and performance. Additionally, new product newness and meaningfulness each positively mediate the effect of digital transforming capability on new product performance.

hot.title: Supply Chain Resilience: A Critical Review of Risk Mitigation, Robust Optimisation, and Technological Solutions and Future Research Directions
hot.venue: Global Journal of Flexible Systems Management
hot.abstract: Abstract This study systematically evaluates the literature of supply chain resilience by integrating bibliometric and network analysis techniques. This analysis is conducted following the dynamic capability, as a theoretical lens, to understand and analyse supply chain resilience. We extracted and curated 294 peer‐reviewed articles from leading academic databases, Web of Science and Scopus, covering the period from January 2000 to 2024. We applied two complementary network analysis methods, a keyword co‐occurrence network (KCON) to analyse the frequency and interrelationships among key terms, and a research focus parallelship network (RFPN) to map the connectivity among research streams. These analytical approaches revealed three distinct research clusters, optimisation for supply chain resilience, technology adoption for supply chain resilience, and resilience strategies against disruptions and risk management. By linking emerging trends in digital transformation with traditional risk management practices, this study offers a new perspective for both academic inquiry and managerial practice. Practically, integrating digital technologies, especially digital twin and machine learning, into risk management processes offers a strategic roadmap for real-time monitoring and decision-making in supply chain resilience. Furthermore, this study identifies significant research gaps, including an exploration of micro‐level dynamics within organisations, and the development of advanced simulation techniques and robust approaches to manage uncertainties.

hot.title: Generative AI and its Transformative Value for Digital Platforms
hot.abstract: The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) represents a watershed moment in the evolution of digital platforms. The capabilities of this AI technology go beyond traditional AI systems, enabling the autonomous generation of novel outcomes with significant implications for platform value creation, architecture, governance, and stakeholder interactions. We develop an integrative conceptual framework that identifies four key mechanisms through which GenAI transforms digital platforms: intelligent automation, democratization, hyper-personalization, and collaborative innovation. Through intelligent automation, GenAI transforms boundary resources from passive interfaces into active, intelligent mediators of value creation. Democratization systematically lowers barriers to platform participation. Hyper-personalization enables dynamic, individual-level adaptation of platform content. Collaborative innovation transforms platform innovation by making GenAI an active participant in human-AI value co-creation. We use this framework to situate the papers in the special issue and develop a research agenda that explores the transformative impact of GenAI on platform stakeholder relationships.

hot.title: Lower Artificial Intelligence Literacy Predicts Greater AI Receptivity
hot.abstract: As artificial intelligence (AI) transforms society, understanding factors that influence AI receptivity is increasingly important. The current research investigates which types of consumers have greater AI receptivity. Contrary to expectations revealed in four surveys, cross-country data and six additional studies find that people with lower AI literacy are typically more receptive to AI. This lower literacy–greater receptivity link is not explained by differences in perceptions of AI's capability, ethicality, or feared impact on humanity. Instead, this link occurs because people with lower AI literacy are more likely to perceive AI as magical and experience feelings of awe in the face of AI's execution of tasks that seem to require uniquely human attributes. In line with this theorizing, the lower literacy–higher receptivity link is mediated by perceptions of AI as magical and is moderated among tasks not assumed to require distinctly human attributes. These findings suggest that companies may benefit from shifting their marketing efforts and product development toward consumers with lower AI literacy. In addition, efforts to demystify AI may inadvertently reduce its appeal.

hot.title: Artificial Intelligence Adoption for Sustainable Growth in SMEs : An Extended Dynamic Capability Framework
hot.venue: Corporate Social Responsibility and Environmental Management
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT The adoption of Artificial Intelligence is transforming enterprises worldwide, influencing various aspects of business operations and affecting all dimensions of the triple bottom line. Companies ready to leverage the potential of this technology can significantly improve their performance. Therefore, it is crucial to understand the relationship between internal capabilities and contextual factors on one hand, and Artificial Intelligence adoption and its impact on performance on the other. Within this research framework, this study introduces an extended dynamic capability framework to analyze the interplay between internal factors, Artificial Intelligence adoption, and companies performance. The proposed model is tested using Partial Least Squares—Structural Equation Modeling on survey data from 210 Italian innovative startups. The findings indicate that companies with well‐developed dynamic capabilities, enabling them to adapt more effectively to environmental changes, are also better equipped to adopt Artificial Intelligence, leading to positive social, economic, and environmental performance.

hot.title: Unveiling triple bottom line's influence on business performance
hot.abstract: Addressing environmental, social, and economic challenges has become a pressing global priority. The Triple Bottom Line (TBL) framework offers a holistic approach for evaluating corporate performance by integrating economic, environmental, and social perspectives. Despite its increasing adoption in both managerial and academic research, there remains a significant gap in understanding how the TBL framework influences business performance. To address this, the study conducts a bibliometric review of 207 publications from the Web of Science database. The review highlights the multifaceted impact of practices linked to the TBL dimensions on business performance while introducing the TBL Influence on Business Performance model. This model provides valuable insights into how businesses can effectively apply TBL principles to address socio-environmental challenges, foster innovation, and achieve sustained long-term performance. The findings contribute valuable theoretical and practical insights into how organizations can utilize TBL principles to strengthen resilience, innovation, and performance in the face of global socio-environmental challenges.

hot.title: What you see is not what you get: ESG scores and greenwashing risk
hot.abstract: This paper shows that ESG scores capture a company’s greenwashing behavior. Greenwashing accusations are most prevalent among large companies with high ESG scores. We empirically employ a novel theoretical model that distinguishes between the communication of a company’s environmental efforts (apparent environmental performance) and its actual environmental impact (real environmental performance). The correlation of the apparent (real) environmental performance with ESG scores is significantly positive (negative). Therefore, ESG scores are unsuitable for measuring real environmental impact. Thus, investors focusing on high ESG-rated companies may unknowingly increase their greenwashing risk exposure, and academics may use misleading information to assess greenwashing risk. • ESG scores are positively correlated with greenwashing cases. • ESG scores mainly measure the apparent rather than the real environmental performance. • Higher analyst coverage limits the exaggeration of apparent environmental performance.

hot.title: Can Generative AI Chatbots Emulate Human Connection? A Relationship Science Perspective
hot.abstract: The development of generative artificial intelligence capable of sustaining complex conversations has created a burgeoning market for companion chatbots promising social and emotional connection. The appeal of these products raises questions about whether chatbots can fulfill the functions of close relationships. Proponents argue that relationships with chatbots can be as meaningful as relationships between humans, whereas critics argue they are a dangerous distraction from genuine connections. This analysis applies theoretical tools from more than 50 years of research on close relationships to evaluate the extent to which human-chatbot interactions meet the definition of and fulfill the functions of close relationships. Interactions between humans and chatbots do possess some characteristic features of close relationships: Humans and chatbots can influence each other and engage in frequent and diverse conversations over time. Chatbots can be responsive in ways humans perceive as supportive, generating feelings of connection and opportunities for growth. Yet because chatbots make only superficial requests of their users, relationships with them cannot provide the benefits of negotiating with and sacrificing for a partner and may reinforce undesirable behaviors. Research that attends to the characteristics of users, chatbots, and their interactions will be crucial for identifying for whom these relationships will be beneficial or harmful.

hot.title: Artificial intelligence technologies and entrepreneurship: a hybrid literature review
hot.abstract: The disruptive potential of artificial intelligence (AI) technologies involves creating new entrepreneurial opportunities and reshaping the entrepreneurial process. The impact of AI technologies on entrepreneurial activity is also reflected in an explosive level of research interest, leading to the fragmentation of existing studies. This phenomenon makes generating a comprehensive and systematic overview challenging. This paper reviews the existing research on the application of AI-based technologies in entrepreneurial practice. Specifically, it conducts a hybrid literature review, analyzing 345 articles from peer-reviewed journals. It identifies the main contributions to the field; the conceptual, social, and intellectual structures; and the leading themes addressed to date. Despite growing interest in the field, this study concludes that most academic research on the subject has been superficial. This study proposes future lines of research based on the antecedents, decisions, and outcomes (ADO) and the theories, contexts, and methods (TCM) frameworks.

hot.title: Sustainability or Greenwashing: Evidence from the Asset Market for Industrial Pollution
hot.abstract: ABSTRACT We study the asset market for pollutive plants. Firms divest pollutive plants in response to environmental pressures. Buyers are firms facing weaker environmental pressures that have supply chain relationships or joint ventures with the sellers. While pollution levels do not decline following divestitures, sellers highlight their sustainable policies in subsequent conference calls, earn higher returns as they sell more pollutive plants, and benefit from higher Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) ratings and lower compliance costs. Overall, the asset market allows firms to redraw their boundaries in a manner perceived as environmentally friendly without real consequences for pollution but with substantial gains from trade.

hot.title: Mapping the greenwashing research landscape: a theoretical and field analysis
hot.abstract: Abstract This study provides a comprehensive overview of greenwashing research in business and management, focusing on its conceptual and theoretical foundations. Through a systematic literature review of 97 peer-reviewed articles from Scopus and Web of Science, we use bibliometric analysis to map the evolution of greenwashing studies and network analysis and identify four thematic clusters: (1) symbolic management and CSR communication, (2) environmental regulations and institutional complexity, (3) performance and sustainable practices, and (4) marketing, perception, and trust. Additionally, we perform a full-text analysis to map the theoretical frameworks employed across these clusters, revealing the dominance of macro-level theories (e.g., legitimacy, institutional, and stakeholder theories) and their cross-level interactions with meso- and micro-level approaches. By developing a multi-level theoretical framework, we provide a structured approach to understanding greenwashing across different analytical layers. Then, focusing on the theories used to investigate greenwashing, we identify some avenues for future research. This study has practical implications for understanding how greenwashing affects corporate governance, financial performance, and stakeholder trust, providing insights for enhancing transparency and accountability in sustainable business practices.

hot.title: Third-party evaluators perceive AI as more compassionate than expert humans
hot.abstract: Empathy connects us but strains under demanding settings. This study explored how third parties evaluated AI-generated empathetic responses versus human responses in terms of compassion, responsiveness, and overall preference across four preregistered experiments. Participants (N = 556) read empathy prompts describing valenced personal experiences and compared the AI responses to select non-expert or expert humans. Results revealed that AI responses were preferred and rated as more compassionate compared to select human responders (Study 1). This pattern of results remained when author identity was made transparent (Study 2), when AI was compared to expert crisis responders (Study 3), and when author identity was disclosed to all participants (Study 4). Third parties perceived AI as being more responsive-conveying understanding, validation, and care-which partially explained AI's higher compassion ratings in Study 4. These findings suggest that AI has robust utility in contexts requiring empathetic interaction, with the potential to address the increasing need for empathy in supportive communication contexts.

hot.title: The past, present, and future of sustainability marketing: How did we get here and where might we go?
hot.abstract: The ever-increasing concerns about global sustainability have sparked intense debates and actions across various sectors, with marketing playing a pivotal role in influencing both the problem and potential solutions. This article maps the historical trajectory of sustainability marketing, analyzes current trends, and explores future directions to enhance sustainability within marketing practice. We show that sustainability marketing has historically centered on resource conservation and green marketing , but in recent years its scope has expanded to encompass a broader range of topics. These include the circular economy , anti-consumption, regulatory frameworks, innovation, carbon emissions , as well as the social and ethical considerations inherent in sustainability marketing. We propose three main areas within which sustainability marketing might expand in the future: system-driven changes, business-driven changes, and consumer-driven changes. Our analysis aims to deepen the understanding of sustainability marketing and inspire marketers to explore questions and solutions that will contribute to a sustainable future.

hot.title: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots for companionship? The relationship between chatbot usage and social connectedness in Danish high-school students
hot.abstract: Are lonely youngsters turning to chatbots to fill their social needs? The present research contributes to the ongoing scientific endeavors to understand the adoption of chatbots as social companions. Specifically, we examined how many Danish high-school students engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots, why they engage in such conversations, and whether this trend is associated with the sense of social connectedness (operationalized as loneliness and perceived social support). In pursuing this goal, a preregistered mixed-methods cross-sectional survey study was carried out. A total sample of 1599 students from 15 Danish high schools was collected. In total, 234 students (14.6%) responded that they engage in friend-like conversations with chatbots. Qualitative thematic analyses of free-text responses revealed two dominant ways of engaging with chatbots: utilitarian conversations (n = 174) and social-supportive conversations (n = 39). A major finding was that social-supportive chatbot users reported significantly more loneliness than non-chatbot users (d = 0.53) and utilitarian chatbot users (d = 0.52). Furthermore, social-supportive chatbot users also reported significantly lower perceived social support than non-chatbot users (d = -0.46). Analyses also showed significant associations between higher loneliness and less perceived social support and various situational triggers for initiating conversations with chatbots, including bad mood, a need for self-disclosure, and a sense of loneliness, but not with a sense of friendship to the chatbot as a trigger of chatbot interactions. These findings suggest a trend among some socially disconnected Danish high-school students toward using chatbots to cope with negative emotions.

latest.title: Exploring the value perceptions of young Indian luxury consumers towards inconspicuous luxury apparel consumption: evidence from homegrown brands
latest.abstract: Purpose With the mass-market proliferation of luxury and the evolving value orientation of millennial Indians, who embrace individualism while remaining part of a larger social framework, a bent towards subtle luxury has been observed. The study seeks to understand the value perceptions of young Indian consumers regarding the consumption of inconspicuous luxury apparel. Design/methodology/approach Data were collected from respondents living in Delhi using purposive sampling (judgemental and snowball), resulting in a total of 326 respondents. Findings The study stipulates that different values, including Individual value, Functional value, Emotional value, Epistemic value and Social value, positively affect the perceptions of contemporary Indian luxury consumers towards inconspicuous luxury apparel choices. Originality/value With the rapidly evolving tastes of contemporary luxury consumers shifting towards high-quality fashion that is more personal than social, the phenomenon of inconspicuous fashion luxury is gaining traction. This holds particular relevance in an emerging economy like India, which in the past favoured the conspicuous display of material wealth through flashy apparel. By applying the theory of consumption values, this study attempts to explore the value perceptions of Indian consumers towards the consumption of inconspicuous luxury apparel. In doing so, it contributes significantly towards the limited understanding of inconspicuous luxury.

latest.title: Incomplete compliance: Loot box prevalence, presence disclosures, probability disclosures, and Compu Gacha policy in Japanese mobile games
latest.abstract: Background and aims: Loot boxes or gacha are bought in video games to obtain randomised rewards. Their gambling-like characteristics and associations with both gambling and videogaming disorder worry parents and regulators. As the third-largest videogaming market, Japan has a decade-long history of regulating loot boxes. Several regulations co-exist. Games must disclose the probabilities of obtaining different random rewards. A particular implementation ('Compu Gacha') that provides an extra reward after players pay to collect a specific combination of two or more other rewards is prohibited. We investigated loot box prevalence amongst Japanese mobile games and whether they complied with various regulations. Methods: In late 2025, we assessed the presence of loot boxes, Compu Gacha, and in-game probability disclosures in the 100 highest-grossing iPhone games in Japan based on the first hour of gameplay from account creation. We also checked whether games disclosed loot box presence on app stores. Results: Amongst 91 games with loot boxes, 17.6 and 33.0% failed to disclose their presence on the Apple App Store and the Google Play Store, respectively. Most games with loot boxes (90.1%) provided probability disclosures for at least one loot box identified, but only 41.8% disclosed probabilities for all loot boxes found. Four games contained suspected Compu Gacha. Discussion and Conclusions: Loot box prevalence is very high amongst Japanese mobile games. Most companies, including local Japanese ones, only partially complied with long-established probability disclosure industry self-regulations. Rare cases of suspected prohibited Compu Gacha were identified. Recent Apple App Store policy and platform design changes significantly improved loot box presence disclosure transpar

latest.title: The relationship between green human resources management (GHRM) and service quality
latest.venue: Silphium Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: In recent decades, human activities have increasingly negatively impacted the environment, driven by factors such as globalization and intensifying competition. In response, a modern approach to Human Resource Management (HRM), known as Green Human Resource Management (GHRM), has emerged. GHRM aims to integrate eco-friendly practices into organizational operations while maintaining business competitiveness. This study contributes to the existing body of knowledge by exploring the impact of GHRM on service quality within small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Tripoli, Libya. A quantitative research methodology was adopted, with data collected through a survey administered to a randomly selected sample of 100 employees working in various SMEs in Tripoli. Ethical approval was obtained from the relevant Libyan authorities, and the surveys were distributed both electronically and in person, in compliance with institutional permissions. The collected data were analyzed using multiple regression analysis to test the study’s hypotheses. The findings indicate that employees in Libyan SMEs possess a moderate understanding of GHRM practices. Furthermore, the results demonstrate a statistically significant positive relationship between GHRM and service quality. Based on these findings, the study recommends that service-oriented industries prioritize the adoption of GHRM practices to enhance service performance, improve organizational outcomes, and promote environmental sustainability.

latest.title: Pemberdayaan UMKM Batik Gama Wening melalui Pengembangan Identitas Merek Berbasis Kearifan Lokal dan Media Pemasaran Digital Berbasis Storytelling
latest.venue: KENDURI Jurnal Pengabdian dan Pemberdayaan Masyarakat
latest.abstract: Batik Gama Wening, a micro, small, and medium enterprise (MSME) located in Pait Village, Kasembon District, Malang Regency, lacks an adequate brand identity and effective digital marketing management. This community service program aimed to develop a brand identity rooted in local wisdom and enhance the partner's capacity to create storytelling-based digital marketing content to support market expansion. The program involved needs assessment, collaborative brand identity development through a co-creation approach, training in storytelling-based digital marketing content development, outcome-based evaluation, and sustainability enhancement. The program outputs included a logo and corporate color scheme reflecting local characteristics, brand identity applications across supporting media, packaging design, a one-month content calendar, and 12 Instagram content packages. The partner also demonstrated the ability to explain the meaning of the brand identity, plan content themes, develop content using Gemini AI, and prepare materials for publication. Periodic monitoring is necessary to assess the consistency of implementation, the partner's management capacity, and the program's contribution to market expansion and sales transactions.

latest.title: Mapping the evolution of carbon accounting and disclosure research through bibliometric analysis
latest.abstract: The intensifying implications of climate change have brought carbon accounting and disclosure to the forefront of policy and scholarly debate, generating an emerging research field that examines its multidimensional nature. Despite the growing body of literature, existing studies remain fragmented and fail to provide a consolidated understanding of the field’s development. This research addresses that gap by conducting a bibliometric examination of 715 Scopus-indexed articles published between 1992 and 2025. Using Biblioshiny and VOSviewer, the study uncovers prominent publication trends, leading authors, and thematic trajectories in carbon accounting research. The results reveal a consistent increase in scholarly output over time, with China identified as the highest contributing nation and journals such as the Journal of Cleaner Production and Sustainability (Switzerland) recognized as the most productive publishing outlets. The most productive author is found to be Professor Tang Q of Western Sydney University. Thematic mapping and co-occurrence analysis highlight six dominant research clusters: Corporate Environmental Disclosure and Performance; Life Cycle and Emission Analysis; Climate Policy and Forest Carbon Sequestration; Technological and Emerging Themes in Carbon Management; Accounting and Methodological Approaches; and Carbon Disclosure, Sustainability, and Regional Empirical Synthesis. This study provides valuable insights into the intellectual structure and thematic evolution of carbon accounting and disclosure research, while offering directions for future inquiry and informing policy discussions in the field.

latest.title: The social self in sustainable luxury services: psychological ownership, identification and willingness to use
latest.abstract: Purpose Drawing on symbolic interactionism, this study aims to examine how social expressiveness influences consumers’ willingness to use sustainable luxury services (SLS). It further investigates the mediating roles of identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being, and the moderating role of psychological ownership. Design/methodology/approach The research uses a two-study design. Study 1 uses survey data from Prolific to test the hypothesized direct, mediation and moderation relationships and to assess the measurement model. Study 2 provides field-based evidence using two Facebook advertisements for a sustainable luxury hotel and click-through rate (CTR) as the behavioral outcome. Study 1 was analyzed using structural equation modeling and moderation analysis. Findings Social expressiveness is positively associated with willingness to use SLS, and this relationship is sequentially mediated by identification with SLS and utilitarian well-being. Psychological ownership significantly moderates the relationships among social expressiveness, identification, utilitarian well-being and willingness to use SLS; however, the negative interaction terms indicate attenuation rather than the hypothesized strengthening. In Study 2, the social-expressiveness advertisement generated a CTR more than 40% higher than the non-social-expressiveness advertisement. Originality/value This research extends luxury service research by showing how a socially expressive motive is translated into willingness to use SLS through identification and well-being. It also positions psychological ownership as a boundary condition in a non-ownership service context, while showing that high psychological ownership can reduce the marginal importance of other drivers of willingness. The study thereby offe

latest.title: Decision pathways in mobile-app shopping: a Throughput Model study of online consumers
latest.abstract: Purpose Mobile shopping environments increasingly rely on artificial intelligence (AI) to personalise recommendations, curate product information and support purchase decisions. Yet, existing consumer decision-making models maintain a linear, stage-based logic that fails to capture how AI-enabled interfaces compress, extend or reconfigure the pathways consumers actually follow. This study aims to use the Throughput Model (TPM) to conceptualise and empirically validate distinct algorithmic decision pathways through which perception, information search and evaluative judgement interact to shape purchase intentions in mobile-app shopping contexts. Design/methodology/approach Survey data were collected from Gen Z consumers with recent mobile-app shopping experience. The study applies partial least squares structural equation modelling and mediation analysis to test the TPM and estimate one-step, two-step and three-step decision pathways in AI-enabled mobile commerce. Findings Perception, information search and judgement each exert significant effects within the model, with judgement emerging as the central integrative mechanism linking upstream inputs to purchase intention. These results demonstrate that AI-enabled mobile interfaces simultaneously support impulsive, efficiency-driven and deliberative decision architectures. Originality/value To the best of the authors’ knowledge, this study provides the first empirical operationalisation of the TPM in mobile-app commerce, reconceptualising purchase decisions as coexisting algorithmic pathways rather than a single sequential route. It offers marketers a diagnostic framework for segmenting consumers by decision architecture and designing adaptive AI-enabled shopping experiences accordingly.

latest.title: Smart Kitchen Counter Innovation for Elderly Users Based on Quality Function Deployment and Internet of Things System
latest.venue: ASEAN Journal of Scientific and Technological Reports
authors: Thaya ธยา ภิรมย์ Pirom
latest.abstract: This study aims to design and develop a kitchen counter product for elderly users by applying the Quality Function Deployment (QFD) technique to address user requirements. The study began with a survey of elderly users’ needs, including design, facilities, usability, product quality, and materials. The collected data was analyzed using the QFD product planning matrix and the design deployment matrix to translate customer requirements into technical design specifications. The results indicated that the participants reported a mean perceived satisfaction score of 4.42 out of 5.00 after observing a demonstration of the prototype and its functions in an actual kitchen environment. The five product attributes with the highest satisfaction scores were lighting within overhead cabinet storage compartments, operational safety, ease of maintenance, structural strength, and electrical outlet safety systems, with mean scores of 4.62, 4.57, 4.56, 4.54, and 4.53, respectively. These findings demonstrate that Quality Function Deployment (QFD) is an effective approach for translating user requirements into product design, particularly in the development of kitchen counter products for elderly users. The resulting design was perceived as having the potential to improve safety and convenience for elderly users during kitchen activities. However, further hands-on usability and long-term field testing are required to verify its effectiveness under actual use conditions.

latest.title: Drivers of sustainable fashion purchase in India: a moderated value framework
latest.abstract: Purpose Although sustainable fashion research has extensively examined either consumer attitudes or purchase intentions, limited studies have explicitly distinguished between the cognitive foundation of attitude and the situationally driven nature of intention within the eco-fashion context. Furthermore, the interactive role of psychological traits such as altruism and mindfulness, along with economic considerations like willingness to pay a premium, in moderating the attitude–intention relationship remains underexplored, particularly in emerging markets such as India. This study aims to address these gaps by developing and empirically validating an integrated framework that captures both individual and contextual drivers of eco-fashion purchase intention. Design/methodology/approach Adopting a comprehensive mixed-methods design informed by grounded theory principles, this study explores the underlying factors that shape the phenomenon. Qualitative data from interviews and FGD enabled themes to emerge inductively, while quantitative survey data validated and extended these insights. Statistical analyses examined relationships among variables, and hypotheses were tested using SEM to ensure robustness of the conceptual model. Findings Environmental consciousness, social influence and marketing stimuli considerably shape eco-fashion attitude and purchase intention, while attitude mediates these relationships. Altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay strengthen the relationship between attitude and purchase intention. Originality/value The study proposes a moderated value framework that explains sustainable fashion purchase more dynamically by treating altruism, mindfulness and willingness to pay as moderators in the Indian context.

latest.title: Tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng của người tiêu dùng trẻ trong mua sắm livestream: bằng chứng từ ngành thời trang Việt Nam
latest.venue: The University of Danang - Journal of Science and Technology
latest.abstract: Trong lĩnh vực livestream thời trang tại Việt Nam, hành vi ra quyết định mua của nhóm khách hàng trẻ chịu ảnh hưởng bởi các tín hiệu xã hội, đặc biệt là cảm giác sợ bỏ lỡ và xu hướng hành động theo đám đông. Dựa trên khung Kích thích – Chủ thể – Phản hồi (S-O-R), nghiên cứu kiểm định tác động của nỗi lo sợ bỏ lỡ (FoMO) và hiệu ứng đám đông đến hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng, đồng thời phân tích vai trò trung gian của trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng. Dữ liệu 308 người tiêu dùng trẻ đã tham gia mua sắm livestream thời trang được phân tích bằng PLS-SEM. Kết quả cho thấy, FoMO và hiệu ứng đám đông đều ảnh hưởng tích cực đến trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy mua sắm bốc đồng và hành vi mua bốc đồng. Trạng thái tâm lý thúc đẩy hành vi mua sắm bốc đồng đóng vai trò trung gian một phần. Nghiên cứu góp phần cung cấp thêm bằng chứng thực nghiệm trong livestream commerce ngành thời trang tại Việt Nam và gợi ý hàm ý quản trị cho doanh nghiệp.

latest.title: Pet insurance services adoption: how values, reasoning, and insurance literacy shape consumer intentions in an emerging market
latest.abstract: Purpose This study aims to examine pet-insurance adoption in India through behavioral reasoning theory (BRT), focusing on how openness to change and social value shape reasons for and against adoption, how these reasons influence attitude and purchase intention and whether insurance literacy strengthens the attitude–intention relationship. Design/methodology/approach A sequential mixed-methods design was used. Interviews with 17 pet owners identified the facilitators and inhibitors. Survey data from 352 respondents were analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling to test the mediation and moderation effects. Demographic moderation was treated as an exploratory analysis. Findings Openness to change strengthened both reasons for and reasons against adoption, whereas social value strengthened supportive reasoning and reduced opposing reasoning. Reasons for adoption positively influenced attitude and intention, whereas reasons against adoption had negative effects. Attitude was the strongest predictor of purchase intention, and insurance literacy strengthened the attitude–intention relationship. The unexpected positive association between openness to change and reasons against adoption suggests that receptiveness to novelty may intensify scrutiny of benefits and barriers instead of uniformly increasing adoption readiness. Research limitations/implications The cross-sectional sample limits the causal inference and generalizability of the findings. Future research should test the deliberative role of openness to change using longitudinal, behavioral and cross-market designs. Practical implications Insurers should address benefits and barriers, including affordability, exclusions, coverage limits and claims procedures, while using pet-insurance education

latest.title: Human Resource Management Strategies for Improving Work Effectiveness and Service Quality: A Case Study
latest.abstract: This study aims to analyze human resource management strategies in improving work effectiveness and service quality at Mubarak Tour & Travel. The study employed a qualitative approach using a case study method. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, direct observation, documentation, and literature review. Informants were selected purposively and included the director, employees, marketing staff, mutawwif, and pilgrims who had used the services of Mubarak Tour & Travel more than twice. Data were analyzed through data reduction, data display, and conclusion drawing and verification using the interactive analysis model of Miles, Huberman, and Saldaña. The findings indicate that Mubarak Tour & Travel faces limitations in its human resource structure, resulting in overlapping responsibilities and increased workload dynamics, particularly during periods of high pilgrim numbers and departure schedules. These challenges are managed through the optimization of available human resources, flexible task allocation, coordination and collaboration among employees, and competency development through briefings, direct guidance, experience sharing, and work evaluation. These strategies contribute to improving productivity, timely task completion, and employees’ ability to adapt to changing workloads. In addition, human resource management contributes to service quality through service reliability, responsiveness, assurance, empathy, and the provision of facilities that meet pilgrims’ needs. The findings further show that service quality is achieved through the integrated roles of the director, employees, marketing staff, and mutawwif throughout the entire process of serving pilgrims.
latest.subfield: Organizational Behavior and Human Resource Management

latest.title: أشهر أخطاء ومزايا قوائم الطعام (المنيو): دراسة مقارنة لعشر حالات تشخيصية في قطاع المطاعم والمشروبات
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: تتناول هذه الورقة سؤالًا عمليًا: ما الأخطاء والمزايا التي تتكرر في قوائم الطعام، وهل يجمعها نمط واحد؟ اعتمدت الدراسة على عشر حالات تشخيصية أعدّها الباحث ونُشرت في «أطلس تشخيص قوائم الطعام» (٢٠٢٦): كباب أوزي، والأكيل، وSmiley Hearts، وMIROLA Cheesecake، وتتبيلة، وع الفحم، وTrifillo Gelato، ومصراوي، وسِكّة، ونينو NENO. قُيّمت كل قائمة نوعيًا على أربعة عشر محورًا وبثلاثة مستويات، وفُرّغت التقييمات (١٤٠ تقييمًا) في مصفوفة مقارنة. تكشف النتائج «فجوة العرض والتوجيه»: تنوع المنتجات والهوية البصرية جاءا «جيد» فأعلى في الحالات العشر كلها، بينما جاء تطبيق ممارسات هندسة القائمة «يحتاج تطوير» في الحالات العشر، ووصف المنتجات وإبرازها في تسع حالات، وعرض الأسعار والبيع الإضافي وعلم نفس المستهلك في سبع حالات لكل منها. ورُصدت كثافة المعلومات أو طول القائمة صراحةً في ثماني حالات. تقترح الورقة ترتيبًا عمليًا لأولويات تطوير القوائم، وتناقش حدود الأدلة النوعية في غياب بيانات المبيعات والتكلفة. Abstract. This working paper asks which strengths and shortcomings recur across restaurant menus. It draws on ten diagnostic cases from the author's Restaurant Menu Diagnostic Atlas (2026), each rated qualitatively on fourteen dimensions (140 ratings). Results show a consistent display–guidance gap: product variety and visual identity were rated good or better in all ten cases, while application of menu-engineering practice needed development in all ten, product descriptions and item highlighting in nine, and price presentation, upselling and consumer-psychology cues in seven each. Information density was flagged explicitly in eight cases. The paper proposes practical priorities for menu redesign and discusses the limits of qualitative evidence without sales and cost data.

latest.title: Revisiting the Relationship Between Celebrity Worship and Intimate Relationship Expectations in Indian and American Adolescents
latest.abstract: The purposes of the present study were to correct some mistakes in a previous study (Jia, 2025) done in China and to attempt to replicate the Chinese findings in the United States and India. In two related studies (India & the United States) we administered a brief version of the Celebrity Attitude Scale (CAS-7), a modified version of the Romantic Beliefs Scale (RBS), and the short version of the Self-Reflection and Insight Scale (SRIS) to late adolescents. We hypothesized, and generally found, that the relationship between admiration for one’s favorite celebrity was positively related to the belief that adult intimate relationships will always remain very romantic. We found no gender difference in Romantic Beliefs scores in either country. A subsample of participants who selected an other-gender favorite celebrity did not score significantly higher on the CAS-7 than those who selected a favorite celebrity of the same gender as the participant. Lower SRIS scores were associated with higher CAS-7 scores and higher RBS scores in both countries. Discussion focused on cultural similarities and differences.

latest.title: Development of a Consumer Behavior-Based Digital Marketing Model to Improve Tourism SME Performance in Kupang City
latest.venue: Journal of Accounting and Finance Management
latest.abstract: Digital marketing has become increasingly important for tourism small and medium-sized enterprises, yet its contribution to business performance may depend on how consumers respond to digital marketing activities. This study aims to examine the effects of digital marketing on consumer behavior and tourism small and medium-sized enterprise performance, as well as the mediating role of consumer behavior in Kupang City. A quantitative explanatory survey was conducted using structured questionnaires and analyzed using partial least squares structural equation modeling. The study involved 33 tourism small and medium-sized enterprise actors and 180 consumers selected through purposive sampling. The results show that digital marketing has a positive and significant effect on consumer behavior and small and medium-sized enterprise performance. Consumer behavior also has a positive and significant effect on small and medium-sized enterprise performance. Furthermore, consumer behavior significantly mediates the relationship between digital marketing and small and medium-sized enterprise performance, indicating complementary mediation. These findings suggest that digital marketing contributes to tourism small and medium-sized enterprise performance both directly and through consumer responses. The contribution of this study lies in integrating digital marketing, consumer behavior, and small and medium-sized enterprise performance within a single empirical model in the tourism context.

latest.title: Study on the Influence Mechanism of Consumers’ Purchase Intention of Pet Products Based on the SOR Theory
latest.abstract: With the vigorous development of the pet economy, an in-depth investigation into consumers’ purchase intention of pet products is crucial to the development of the industry. Based on the SOR (Stimulus-Organism-Response) theory, this paper constructs a research model of consumers’ purchase intention of pet products and puts forward the following hypotheses: external stimuli such as product factors positively affect emotional responses; external stimuli such as product factors positively affect cognitive evaluation; and emotional responses and cognitive evaluation positively affect purchase intention respectively. Data were collected through questionnaire design, and empirical analysis was conducted by means of descriptive statistics, confirmatory factor analysis, multiple linear regression and other methods. The empirical results show that marketing activities enhance confidence in consumption decisions, purchase situations improve users’ sense of pleasure, product factors strengthen cognitive rationality, marketing activities optimize consumption risk assessment, purchase situations improve the judgment of scheme feasibility, and both consumers’ emotions and cognition exert a positive driving effect on purchase intention. This paper enriches the application of the SOR theory in the field of pet product consumption, and provides a scientific basis for enterprises to optimize product design, formulate marketing strategies and enhance consumers’ purchase intention.

latest.title: SCALE, CHANNEL STRUCTURE AND EFFICIENCY OF RETAIL TRADE SERVICES IN UZBEKISTAN
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The article examines how the size structure of retail enterprises, the shift between sales channels and the composition of consumer demand determine the efficiency of retail trade services in Uzbekistan. The study draws on official statistics of the National Statistics Committee and analytical data for 2016-2025. Turnover per enterprise, the relative labour productivity of trade, compound annual growth rates and arc elasticities of retail turnover with respect to household credit and deposits are calculated. In 2025, the 344 large retail enterprises generated an average turnover of 238.2 billion UZS each, 51 times more than small enterprises and micro-firms (4.67 billion UZS). The share of markets in retail turnover fell from 69% in 2016 to 48% in 2025, while e-commerce reached only 4.7%. Trade accounts for 10.1% of employment but about 6.1% of GDP, which places labour productivity in trade at roughly 60% of the economy-wide average. The arc elasticity of retail turnover with respect to retail loans for 2019–2025 equals 0.72. The results justify measures aimed at consolidating retail services into chain formats, developing omnichannel sales and raising labour productivity in small retail enterprises.

latest.title: The Influence of Utilitarian Values and Flash Sale Method on Women's Skincare Online Purchase Decisions with the Moderation of Joy of Missing Out (JOMO)
latest.abstract: Purpose: This study aims to analyze the influence of Utilitarian Values and the Flash Sale Method on online purchase decisions for women's skincare products on Shopee, as well as to examine the role of the Joy of Missing Out (JOMO) as a moderating variable. Research Method: A quantitative approach with an associative research design was employed. The sample consisted of 110 female consumers who had previously purchased skincare products via Shopee. Data were collected using questionnaires and analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling-Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS). Results and Discussion: The results indicate that Utilitarian Values have a positive and significant effect on online purchase decisions. These findings suggest that the greater the functional benefits perceived by consumers, such as cost savings, convenience, affordability, and added benefits, the higher the likelihood of them making a purchase decision. The Flash Sale Method also has a positive and significant effect on online purchase decisions; factors such as discount magnitude, promotional frequency, duration, product availability, and promotional appeal effectively drive consumer purchasing decisions. Furthermore, JOMO acts as a positive though statistically insignificant moderator in the relationship between Utilitarian Values and online purchase decisions, so the tendency of JOMO to strengthen this relationship has not been statistically proven. Meanwhile, JOMO acts as a negative and statistically significant moderator in the relationship between the Flash Sale Method and online purchase decisions. These findings indicate that JOMO tends to reduce consumer sensitivity to flash sale stimuli. Implications: The research results provide some practical implications for skincare business players and mar

latest.title: ACCOUNTING, AUDIT, AND DIRECTIONS FOR IMPROVING THE MARKETING POLICY OF A FOOD-INDUSTRY ENTERPRISE: THE CASE OF NESTLÉ UKRAINE LLC
latest.abstract: The article substantiates methodological approaches to organizing the accounting and internal audit of marketing expenses of a food-industry enterprise using the example of Nestlé Ukraine LLC. It reveals the composition of marketing expenses recorded as selling expenses, including advertising and marketing communications, advertising agency services, promotion in social media and digital channels, exhibitions and promotional campaigns, trade marketing, merchandising, and logistics support for product distribution. The need for detailed analytical accounting of these expenses by the company's brand portfolio (Svitoch, Torchyn, Mivina, NESCAFÉ, KitKat) is substantiated, since their generalized reflection limits management's ability to assess the return on specific marketing investments. Problematic aspects of the current accounting system are identified: insufficient brand-level detail, difficulty in separating advertising, logistics, and trade-marketing expenses, and a weak link between accounting data and marketing analytics. It is established that over the period under study selling expenses grew significantly, reflecting substantial investment in marketing activity, yet despite rising net sales revenue the company continued to incur a net loss. A plan and program for the internal audit of marketing activity are developed, covering verification of advertising and key-brand promotion costs, digital-marketing accounting, evaluation of trade-marketing effectiveness, and analysis of marketing budget execution. A set of organizational and economic measures for improving the marketing policy is proposed, including detailed brand-level analytical accounting, introduction of the ROMI indicator, strengthened internal audit, improved management reporting, consumer-preference res

latest.title: Easy listing, hard selling? How AI-source disclosure in second-hand product descriptions shapes purchase intention
latest.abstract: Generative AI is increasingly used to create product descriptions in consumer-to-consumer (C2C) online second-hand markets, yet the effects of disclosing the description source remain unclear. Drawing on information diagnosticity theory, this research examines how AI- versus seller-source disclosure affects purchase intention. Across four online experiments, AI-source disclosure reduces purchase intentions in second-hand but not primary markets. This effect is sequentially mediated by perceived information diagnosticity and trust in sellers and is stronger for experience than search products. The negative effect is attenuated when AI is disclosed as being used only for proofreading or when AI-generated descriptions are reviewed by the seller. These findings identify C2C second-hand transactions as a context in which AI-source disclosure can backfire and inform the design of AI-assisted platform listing functions.

latest.title: ANALISIS PENGARUH UGC (USER GENERATED CONTENT) DAN BGC (BRAND GENERATED CONTENT) TERHADAP BRAND AUTHENTICITY MELALUI PURCHASE INTENTION PADA KLAPPERTAART KAWANUA MANADO
latest.venue: JURNAL RISET EKONOMI, MANAJEMEN, BISNIS DAN AKUNTANSI
latest.abstract: This study aims to examine and analyze the effects of User Generated Content (UGC) and Brand Generated Content (BGC) on Brand Authenticity, both directly and indirectly through Purchase Intention as a mediating variable among consumers of Klappertaart Kawanua Manado. A quantitative explanatory design was applied using an online Likert-scale questionnaire survey. A sample of 160 respondents was selected via purposive sampling. Data were analyzed using Structural Equation Modeling based on Partial Least Squares (SEM-PLS) executed in SmartPLS software version 4.2.9. The empirical findings reveal that: (1) UGC has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention; (2) BGC has a positive and significant effect on Purchase Intention; (3) UGC has a positive and significant effect on Brand Authenticity; (4) BGC has a positive and significant effect on Brand Authenticity; (5) Purchase Intention has a positive and significant effect on Brand Authenticity; (6) Purchase Intention partially mediates the effect of UGC on Brand Authenticity; and (7) Purchase Intention partially mediates the effect of BGC on Brand Authenticity. All hypotheses (H1–H7) were supported. Overall, BGC exerts a more dominant influence than UGC in driving purchase intention and enhancing perceived brand authenticity. Culinary MSMEs should combine professional, transparent official brand messaging with customer endorsements to sustain competitive advantage. Keywords: User Generated Content, Brand Generated Content, Purchase intention, Brand Authenticity, Social Media.

latest.title: Modeling Circularwashing Risk in Renewable Energy Adoption: A Structural Equation Approach for Sustainable Consumption
latest.abstract: Abstract Circularwashing limits eco-friendly consumption by overstating, confusing, or inadequately proving the circular properties of products. While regular greenwashing makes ambiguous claims about the environmental characteristics, circularwashing takes advantage of the complicated nature of resource loops and the quality of the supply chain, causing significant market friction and high information asymmetry. Hence, an unexpected change in information distorts price signals, weakens customer trust, and jeopardizes market transparency by creating a lemon market for real circular goods. The present research presents the idea of circularwashing risk and provides a model to analyze the effect of false claims on the customers’ skepticism, decision-making risk perception, institutional trust, penalties for unreasonable behavior, and post-decision actions. The model is based on the Signaling Theory and the Stimulus Organism Response theory and is verified with the help of the survey data collected from 607 digital consumers in Colombia using the method of Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Model (PLS SEM). The measurement properties were assessed through composite reliability, average variance extracted, and heterotrait monotrait discriminant criteria and bootstrap resampling. The findings imply that misleading environmental claims correlate with consumer skepticism, which has a positive relationship with perceived decision risks and the erosion of institutional trust. Moreover, the effects of perceived decision risk and erosion of institutional trust on behavioral penalty are considerable. Structural chains indicate that the relationship between decision risk and erosion of trust serves as two mediating channels. Lastly, the Circularwashing Risk Propagation Model s

latest.title: From landlocked to linked: how the China–Europe Railway Express attracts foreign investment
latest.abstract: Purpose International transportation networks are crucial to global capital allocation. This study aims to examine whether and how the China–Europe Railway Express (CR Express) attracts foreign direct investment (FDI) to connected Chinese cities. It identifies the causal effect of railway connectivity on FDI; investigates trade expansion, industrial upgrading and financial development as potential mechanisms; and explores variations across cities with different economic sizes, urban scales and industrial structures. Design/methodology/approach Using panel data for 285 Chinese prefecture-level cities from 2003 to 2022, this study treats the staggered launch of the CR Express as a quasi-natural experiment and applies a staggered difference-in-differences model to estimate its effect on inward FDI. Parallel trends test, instrumental-variable tests and other a range of robustness tests assess robustness and endogeneity. Mechanism and heterogeneity analyses examine transmission channels and differences across cities. Findings The research results show that the launching of the CR Express has significantly increased the inflow of FDI to cities along the route. The conclusion is still valid after many robustness tests. Mechanism analysis shows that the CR Express may influence FDI through three potential channels: expanding trade scale, upgrading industrial structure and promoting financial development. Further analysis found that this positive impact is more obvious in economically less-developed cities, service-oriented cities and small- and medium-sized cities. Originality/value This study extends FDI location theory by showing how cross-border railway connectivity can offset inland geographical disadvantages and reshape the spatial distribution of foreign investment. It br

latest.title: The Economics of Agri-Food Supply Chain Resilience: Pandemics, Climate Shocks and Global Disruptions
latest.abstract: Agri-food supply chain resilience has become a central economic concern as disease outbreaks, climatic extremes, trade restrictions and geopolitical disruptions expose interdependencies between production, processing, logistics, markets and household food access. Yet operational continuity alone is an incomplete measure of resilience: firms may recover output while consumers face unaffordable diets, workers lose earnings and costly buffers transfer risks between regions or supply-chain tiers. This critical narrative review examines how shocks propagate through agri-food systems, why decentralised incentives may diverge from social welfare, and which private and public responses are supported by credible evidence. Peer-reviewed empirical studies, theoretical analyses, simulations and substantive reviews published from 2004 to 4 September 2026 were assessed through targeted scholarly discovery, bibliographic verification and thematic appraisal, with earlier conceptual antecedents considered where necessary. The synthesis distinguishes covariate from localised shocks, physical scarcity from purchasing-power failures, and short-term recovery from economically and environmentally sustainable adaptation. Pandemic evidence indicates heterogeneous disruptions: substantial losses for particular workers, farmers and perishable-product channels coexisted with adaptive capacity in other markets. Climate research supports material agricultural supply risks, although uncertainty remains about cross-sector transmission and simultaneous harvest failures. Trade and conflict studies indicate that diversification can buffer geographically specific losses but may propagate correlated shortages and policy-induced price instability. latest.title: TRANSITIONING TO A CIRCULAR ECONOMY: STRATEGIES FOR WASTE REDUCTION AND VALUE CREATION
latest.venue: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
latest.abstract: The transition to a circular economy has emerged as an important strategy for addressing environmental challenges, improving resource efficiency, and promoting sustainable economic development. Unlike the traditional linear economic model, which follows a “take–make–dispose” approach, a circular economy seeks to maintain the value of products, materials, and resources for as long as possible. This article examines the fundamental principles of the circular economy and explores practical strategies for waste reduction and value creation across industrial, commercial, and consumer sectors. Particular attention is given to eco-design, recycling, reuse, remanufacturing, industrial symbiosis, sustainable consumption, and digital technologies. The article also analyzes the economic, environmental, and institutional barriers that may hinder the transition toward circular production and consumption patterns. It argues that successful implementation requires coordinated action by governments, businesses, research institutions, and consumers, supported by effective legislation, investment, innovation, and public awareness. The circular economy can contribute to sustainable development by reducing resource dependence, minimizing environmental pressure, creating employment opportunities, and generating new sources of economic value.

latest.title: An Intelligent Multi-objective Decision Support Model for Sustainable Remanufacturing
latest.venue: Process Integration and Optimization for Sustainability
latest.abstract: Remanufacturing offers small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) viable pathways towards transitioning to a circular economy; however, intelligent decision-making systems are needed to accelerate its adoption. Balancing the economic, environmental, and social dimensions of sustainability requires the use of analytical tools that can handle multi-dimensional complexity. This study presents a multi-objective optimization model where remanufacturing tasks are allocated to machines in a factory on the basis of minimizing costs, emissions, and noise exposure. Tri-objective optimization has been carried out using the quadrant shrinking method, and Pareto optimal solutions are translated to an implementation framework that can equip SMEs with an intelligent tool for circular economy adoption. In addition to this, we propose an implementation framework for circular economy in manufacturing based on the DMAIC (define, measure, analyze, improve, and control) approach.

latest.title: Equity Research and Fundamental Analysis of Reliance Industries Limited: Financial Performance, DCF Valuation and Portfolio Relevance for the ABSLI Maximizer ULIP Fund
latest.venue: International Journal of Creative and Open Research in Engineering and Management
latest.abstract: The study evaluates Reliance Industries Limited (RIL) using fundamental equity-research techniques and examines the relevance of the company as a core blue-chip holding in the ABSLI Maximizer ULIP Fund. The research problem arises from the need to assess a diversified conglomerate whose businesses differ materially in growth drivers, capital intensity, risk and cash-flow characteristics. Four objectives were addressed: analysis of five-year financial performance and ratios; construction of an FCFF-based DCF valuation; assessment of RIL’s strategic portfolio relevance; and application of practical wealth-management workflows such as goal discovery, risk profiling and consultative product communication. The study uses a descriptive and analytical research design, a purposive single-company case-study approach, and secondary data from RIL financial statements, investor disclosures, regulatory sources and financial databases. Analysis covers FY2022–FY2026, with DCF projections through FY2031. Results show revenue CAGR of approximately 10.6%, PAT CAGR of about 9.0%, OCF CAGR of about 14.8%, improving ROE and ROCE, moderate leverage and strong cash generation. The base-case DCF estimates intrinsic value at about ₹1,080 per share versus an assumed market price of ₹1,275.90, implying approximately 15.3% downside. The study therefore concludes that RIL has strong fundamentals but requires valuation discipline and continuous monitoring of capital allocation, cash flows and emerging businesses.

latest.title: Green or Greenwashed? Eco-Anxiety and Teen Consumer Choice
latest.venue: Critical Debates in Humanities Science and Global Justice
latest.abstract: Prior research has found that environmental anxiety is becoming prominent among teenagers and can increase their green purchasing intentions. To appeal to growing consumer interest, many companies use greenwashing, a deceptive environmental marketing tactic to appeal to interested consumers but keep their product costs low by avoiding actual eco-friendly production. This tricks worried consumers into believing they are purchasing eco-friendly products when they are not. A survey was conducted to see if there was correlation between how teens analyzed and selected between eco-friendly versus greenwashed product advertisements and their measured eco-anxiety levels. The survey showed low eco-anxiety levels had no association with product selections, medium eco-anxiety levels had notable association with greenwashed selections, and high eco-anxiety levels had notable association with eco-friendly selections. The association between moderate eco-anxiety and greenwashed selections highlights why greenwashing poses an issue to teens who want to make green purchases. However, it is unlikely that the study’s results are highly generalized to a larger population, and the survey should be replicated on a larger scale for better results.

latest.title: Bridging the intention–behavior gap in green fashion: evidence from an emerging market
latest.abstract: Purpose The purpose of this study is to examine the impact of Environmental Concern and Perceived Value; along with its four dimensions, on green fashion Purchase Intention in Egypt, as well as exploring whether an intention-behavior gap exists in this context. It aims to address the limited research on sustainable consumption in the MENA region. Design/methodology/approach A positivist philosophy and deductive approach were adopted. A structured questionnaire, prepared in both English and Arabic, was distributed online, yielding 424 valid responses. Data were analyzed using SPSS for descriptive statistics and SmartPLS 4 for Structural Equation Modeling (SEM). Findings Results show that environmental concern and perceived value significantly impact green fashion purchase intention. However, regarding the dimensions of perceived value, only perceived quality and emotional values had a significant impact, while perceived price and social values did not. Purchase intention was also found to significantly impact actual purchase behavior, suggesting an evidence of intention translating into self-reported purchase behavior within this sample in Egypt’s green fashion sector. Practical implications It is evident that marketers of green fashion in Egypt should emphasize on environmental, quality, and emotional benefits in their marketing strategies. Additionally, it is important for policymakers and stakeholders in the industry to promote environmental awareness as well as provide information regarding the environmental benefits of green fashion products. Furthermore, since the intention-behavior link is significant, it is imperative to ensure that consumers have easy access to green fashion products. Originality/value This study contributes to the green fashion literature by de

latest.title: Reducing the Effect of the Seven Green Wastes Through Green Target Costing for Promoting Sustainability
latest.venue: Indonesian Journal of Law and Economics Review
latest.abstract: General Background Proactive environmental cost management during early product design is crucial for curtailing manufacturing waste and ecological degradation. Specific Background In Iraq's manufacturing sector, the Seven Green Wastes (SGW) remain significant environmental burdens rarely addressed in pre-production accounting. Knowledge Gap Empirical evidence linking Green Target Costing (GTC) to specific waste reduction and quantifiable sustainability performance in Iraqi textile firms remains acutely limited. Aims This study investigates GTC's capability to eliminate SGW during the design stage and its subsequent impact on sustainable performance. Results Utilizing PLS-SEM on survey data from 46 managers, the analysis confirmed GTC explains 57.4% of the variance in SGW elimination, which in turn drives 40.8% of the variance in achieving sustainable corporate outcomes. Novelty This research demonstrates that converting qualitative environmental compliance into design-stage financial parameters transforms ecological side-effects into controllable, eliminable operational losses. Implications Manufacturing managers must embed environmental cost metrics into initial target costing phases to systematically internalize waste reduction, securing both operational cost savings and long-term sustainability. Highlights: Integrating environmental parameters during early product design transforms ecological degradation into controllable, quantifiable production losses. Applying proactive financial strategies at the design stage accounts for over half the variance in eliminating operational manufacturing waste. Systematically curtailing energy, water, and material losses directly drives robust improvements in overall corporate sustainability performance. Keywords: Green Target Cost

latest.title: Operationalizing Precrastination through Scientific Reconstruction
latest.abstract: Most precrastination studies focus on international experience, while the few Russian publications primarily rely on experimental methods. Further domestic analysis of precrastination requires alternative psychodiagnostic tools. Precrastination denotes behavior motivated by the desire to urgently complete current tasks to ensure future comfort by minimizing the cognitive and emotional burden caused by these tasks. The article operationalizes this definition via scientific reconstruction. The results of a written survey (n = 92, aged 17–25) were combined with the semantic differential method and processed statistically using analysis of variance (ANOVA), the Kruskal–Wallis test, and Pearson’s correlation analysis. The survey evaluated the experience of completing tasks as quickly as possible to identify the motivations behind this urgency, as well as to determine its underlying resources. Precrastination proved to be a common phenomenon among young people, exhibiting both universal and specific components across varying degrees of urgency. A pronounced desire for urgency correlated with a clear, resource-based life strategy, while moderate and weak aspirations corresponded with a compensatory-economizing life strategy. Therefore, precrastination may serve as a marker of life agency.

latest.title: Do inclusive retailers build stronger customer relationships? Evidence from a multi-wave repeated cross-sectional study
latest.venue: Journal of Retailing and Consumer Services
latest.abstract: Retailers increasingly adopt diversity, equity, inclusion, and accessibility (DEIA) initiatives, yet limited evidence exists on whether and how consumers translate awareness of these initiatives into stronger customer relationships. Drawing on signaling theory, this study examines whether awareness of retailers' DEIA initiatives is associated with trust and loyalty, and whether this mechanism is consistent across annual samples and forms of diversity. Using a multi-wave repeated cross-sectional survey fielded across seven annual waves from 2019 to 2025, results show that awareness of DEIA initiatives is positively associated with trust, and trust is strongly associated with loyalty. The mechanism is consistent across all annual samples, while the magnitude varies to some extent. Although the results show variation across diversity forms, the trust-loyalty link remains consistently strong. These findings suggest that DEIA initiatives can operate as market signals for retailers’ broader customer base, with effects extending beyond the groups directly targeted by the initiatives. The study contributes to inclusive retailing research by connecting DEIA awareness with customer relationship outcomes and by showing that interventions should not be treated as interchangeable. For managers, the results highlight the importance of visible and context-sensitive DEIA initiatives embedded in the retail customer experience to support positive outcomes.
